### Actual functionality

- New English `/lab-reversals-ui/`, existing common navigation/review index
  and original-editor deep-link reopening; now13 lab endpoint families.
  User explicitly chooses an existing synthetic `FinanceDraftJournal` and
  saved revision. No operational `JournalEntry` source and no fall back to
  current revision or invented historical snapshot.
- GET `/lab/reversal-sources/<journal-id>/<revision>/` returns the immutable
  historical source read-only. Existing foundation database trigger protects
  source snapshots. Proposal/history source FKs PROTECT both current and
  prior linked revisions, including after explicit relinking.
- Explicit date/explanation and2–200 manually entered lines: draft accounts,
  optional BU/dimension selections and both exact debit/credit strings
  (explicit zero allowed). No copied/inverted source lines, defaults, sign/
  date/account mappings, generated entries, fiscal periods or approvals.
  Input bounds are technical lab validation, not company acceptance policy.
- Exact QAR totals/difference and source-offset explanation: combine debit
  minus credit by **account ID + BU ID + sorted dimension-value IDs** across
  source/proposal. “Offsets” requires source and proposal balanced/valid and
  every combined bucket net zero. Splitting lines/memos/order do not affect
  this arithmetic comparison; equal global totals with different buckets
  do not offset. No line-by-line swapping or accounting approval inferred.
  Unbalanced/both-sided/zero-line drafts can be saved with explicit review
  issues and offsets=false, consistent with existing draft-only review.
  Invalid decimals/dates/IDs/entity references reject without partial writes.
- Real save/list/reopen/edit, expected-revision409 conflicts retaining local
  work, source-linked immutable historical snapshots. New proposal revision
  can explicitly change link; old revisions keep their original source.
  Database trigger rejects UPDATE/DELETE of reversal revision history.
- Existing actor/entity/request create receipt/status/replay protocol reused
  unchanged: atomically commit proposal/history/receipt, exact identical replay,
  conflicting reuse409, metadata-only lookup. Current lab guard on every API.
  No new shared permissions, assignments, defaults or grants.
- Source freshness guards suppress obsolete successes/errors. Review found/
  fixed a new UI loading defect: clearing selection while GET pending left
  phantom loading because obsolete finally could not clear it. Explicit
  source/reset/open/access cleanup now clears owned loading. Dirty inputs
  explicitly say they are excluded from the saved server comparison; invalid/
  mismatched source blocks save. Validation/transient/conflict errors preserve
  local input; existing403 clearing and dirty/pending unload safeguards remain.

### Guarantee limits / remaining work

Within a retained database and supplied actor/entity/request identity, tested
identical concurrent/replayed creates commit once. **Not universal exactly-once**:
new/forgotten IDs, unavailable/cleared storage, direct legacy callers without
the header, deleted/restored databases and permanent disaster recovery are
outside that guarantee. Tab payloads are not durably stored; status checking
can survive reload with metadata, executable replay cannot if input is lost.
Receipt original JSON stays protected; status only exposes safe metadata.
No receipt expiry/retention policy invented. Original acknowledged results
are not current-revision snapshots. Browser uses real test sessions, not
ordinary approved Finance authentication; injected post-commit delivery loss
is not a production outage test. Only advance/invoice editor journeys were
native-tested this batch; all12 families share wrapper/review coverage plus
existing full relevant Finance regression suites—not every type's new link
separately exercised in a real browser. Desktop/mobile are specified fixtures,
not all devices/native pickers/screen readers.

### Actual delivered scope

English-only `/lab-adjustments-ui/`, linked from `/lab-ui/`, uses the existing
explicit synthetic Django test-session boundary. Proposal classification starts
unselected: the reviewer must choose credit or debit. Explicit synthetic
supplier/document references, valid proposal date, reason, optional selected
invoice-proposal link, and 1–200 descriptive QAR lines using existing saved
draft accounts/optional BU/dimensions. No supplier master/directory authority
is inferred. Raw descriptions/references, including stored Arabic input, remain
unchanged; internal controls are English.

Amounts are **explicit non-negative magnitudes**, not signed adjustments.
Existing exact decimal-string validation (at most two places, individual
maximum 999999999999.99, technical rather than policy limits) is reused;
Decimal/BigInt-cents totals remain exact. Credit/debit is a reviewer-selected
classification, not an accounting sign convention or inferred account mapping.
Review says proposed=true; issued_credit_note, settlement,
operational_payable_adjustment, approved and posted=false. No change to
operational balances, invoices, journals, stock, payments or accounting policy.

Invoice linking is optional and never inferred; no supplier/line autofill.
Every save validates the current linked invoice is synthetic, in the same
entity and has an exactly matching supplier reference apart from surrounding
ASCII whitespace (case-sensitive). Both UI/server use that same comparison.
The save locks the draft and source invoice and records minimal link evidence:
invoice ID, saved revision and supplier/invoice references. It never changes
the invoice or its history. Link evidence is **validated-at-save historical
evidence**, not live tracking: later invoice edits do not rewrite prior
adjustment revisions; an adjustment edit revalidates against the current
invoice. Explicitly removing/changing a link creates a new adjustment revision.

Real disposable PostgreSQL save/list/reopen/edit, atomic header/history writes,
immutable database-protected revisions and optimistic revision conflicts.
409 retains local work until confirmed reload; 400 retains inputs; 403 clears
protected state. Missing choices are displayed for explicit correction. Dirty
navigation and busy protection retained. Unknown transport/5xx save outcome
blocks blind save/new replacement until explicit register inspection and
reopen. There is **no durable create idempotency/status lookup or exactly-once
creation guarantee**; an empty observed list cannot exclude a delayed commit.
No automatic retry, sign conversion, invoice settlement or scheduling.

English-only `/lab-invoices-ui/`, now linked from `/lab-ui/`, reuses the
existing explicit synthetic Django test session. Manual supplier/invoice
references, explicit valid invoice date and optional independently entered due
date; no due-date derivation or imposed relation between those dates. References
are not approved supplier master identities. Raw descriptions/references,
including user-entered Arabic content and whitespace, remain unchanged.

One to200 descriptive lines with explicit non-negative QAR strings, at most
two decimal places and individual maximum999999999999.99 (technical input
bounds, not accounting policy). Backend Decimal/frontend BigInt-cents totals
remain exact, including aggregate amounts beyond that individual bound.
Each line requires an existing same-entity synthetic draft account; optional
saved BU/dimension references use the existing draft consistency checks.

approval, payment or posting is inferred. Review explicitly reports proposed
true, operational payable/approved/posted false; it does not construct

Real PostgreSQL save/list/reopen/edit, header/history atomicity, row locking,
expected revisions and database-enforced immutable snapshots. A conflicting
409 retains local edits until explicit confirmed reload.400 leaves editable
inputs;403 removes protected state. Fresh context is checked before saving;
missing saved choices remain visible for correction, never substituted.
Transport/5xx uncertainty blocks blind resave/new replacement until explicit
saved-list inspection and reopening. No durable create identity/status lookup,
exactly-once creation or eventual-commit guarantee is claimed; a momentarily
empty list cannot rule out a delayed commit.

Current saved proposals with matching supplier/invoice references produce a
server-side advisory. Comparison is case-sensitive after surrounding ASCII
whitespace removal only, scoped to the same synthetic entity, excluding self,
ordered byID; returned matches contain onlyID/revision. Originals are retained.
The warning neither blocks nor merges duplicates and is not a company
uniqueness rule, fuzzy supplier identity resolver or atomic concurrent-create
guarantee. It refreshes on saved-detail load/save, not on each unsaved keystroke,
and is not written into immutable historical snapshots.

## Previously completed batch — isolated manual cash-forecast scenario drafts

### Delivered behavior and explicit conventions

English-only `/lab-forecasts-ui/`, linked from `/lab-ui/`, uses the existing
explicit synthetic test session. Named scenario, explicit opening QAR balance/
as-of date, manually dated inflow/outflow amounts/descriptions and optional
existing active synthetic BU/saved draft dimensions. No account required or
inferred. Raw descriptions/name/Arabic business content preserved.

- Exact decimal backend and BigInt-cent client arithmetic: opening, total
  inflows/outflows, net change, closing and per-row running balances. Negative
  opening/running/closing balances valid; they are not credit/overdraft authority
  or actual available funds. Row direction supplies the sign of a nonnegative
  explicit amount. Zero allowed. No floats, rounding, exponent notation or FX.
- Amount magnitude <=999999999999.99 per input, at most2 decimals; derived
  totals can exceed that individual technical bound.1–200 rows is a technical
  worksheet limit, not an operative cash/approval rule.
- Source array retained. Review sorts date ascending, then **original input
  position** for equal dates; line number links review back to source. Opening
  is the start of the proposed as-of sequence; same-date flows allowed and rows
  before that date rejected. This is **presentation only**, not intraday timing,
  execution, payment priority, a banking calendar or collection likelihood.
- Real disposable PostgreSQL register/save/list/reopen/edit with immutable
  complete snapshots, atomic history/header updates, row locking and
  expected-revision409 preserving local edits. Confirmed reload explicit.
  Foreign/inactive BU and foreign dimensions rejected server-side; unavailable
  stored choices remain visible for explicit correction, no substitution.
- Current unknown-save behavior retained: transport/5xx after a write attempt
  blocks blind resave/new replacement until explicit saved-list inspection/
  reopen. No durable creation identity/status lookup or exactly-once guarantee;
  an empty list at one instant cannot exclude a delayed commit. Acknowledged
  save plus transient list-refresh failure is not mislabeled an unknown write.
  400 preserves editable inputs;403 clears protected state.
- Explicitly proposed, not actual cash, approved, scheduled or posted. No real
  bank/financial data, connections/imports, automatic AR/AP/quote sourcing,
  inferred collection/payment timing, mappings, terms, tax, FX or approvals.

  save is reported as a saved record with list-refresh failure—not failed write.

  create-request identity/status lookup or exactly-once guarantee. An empty list
  at one instant does not prove a delayed create cannot commit; ambiguous
  outcomes can still require waiting/operator review.

**Complete and verified in isolation, not operational bank reconciliation.**
English `/lab-reconciliation-ui/`, reached from `/lab-ui/` using the existing
explicit synthetic session. Manually entered dated QAR statement/book balances,
source rows and explanations; manually proposed full-row matches; exact
differences and unmatched IDs referencing the preserved source rows. Real
disposable PostgreSQL save/list/reopen/edit, immutable history and conflict
recovery. No session-only persistence substitution.

**New final evidence:** 10 focused / 69 relevant Finance PostgreSQL tests;
11 focused reconciliation UI/helper + 32 existing affected Finance UI tests
(43 unique frontend cases); 2 actual authenticated real-backend browser journeys
at 1280px/390px; 236 contrast checks. Typecheck, main/prototype builds,
Django/system/schema/migration and final diff checks pass. Details, initial

### Implemented comparison and persistence boundaries

- Explicit statement and book snapshot dates/balances, proposal name/explanation,
  fixed QAR, and 0–100 manually entered rows per source. Each source row has a
  local proposal ID, explicit calendar date/magnitude/increase-or-decrease
  direction, original reference and explanation. Local IDs are not an assumed
  bank-reference format. Zero magnitudes and signed balances are numeric proposal
  inputs, not policies about transactions/overdrafts. No direction/date is inferred.
- One-to-one **complete-row** proposed matches require equal exact magnitude and
  direction; a row cannot be used twice. Different dates/references may be
  manually paired. Duplicate, incompatible, missing and dangling pairs cannot
  save. Unmatch explicitly before removing a referenced source. No grouping,
  partial/net matching, tolerance, account mapping or automatic adjustment.
- Row net = increases minus decreases. Balance difference = statement snapshot
  minus book snapshot. Unmatched-row difference = unmatched statement net minus
  unmatched book net. Comparison residual = balance difference minus
  unmatched-row difference. Different balance dates show an arithmetic-only
  advisory. Source sets are not assumed complete or bounded by a bank cutoff;
  balances are not opening balances. **Zero residual is never a reconciled,
  approved or posted account.**
- Decimal strings/Python Decimal and frontend bigint cents preserve exact
  quantities; amounts have at most two decimals and input magnitude below
  QAR 1,000,000,000,000.00 (a technical field limit, not a commercial limit).
  Original references/explanations, including supplied Arabic content and
  whitespace, are retained. Internal UI remains English.
- Atomic header/revision saves, row locks and expected revisions prevent lost
  updates. Database trigger rejects revision UPDATE/DELETE. A 409 keeps local
  inputs until explicit confirmed saved-version reload. Validation failures
  retain work. Network/5xx uncertainty blocks blind resave/new replacement;
  manual saved-list inspection/reopen is required, not automatic retry or
  exactly-once-create proof. Post-commit unrelated list-refresh failure does
  not mislabel a committed save; confirmed 403 clears protected state.
- Guarded lab-only migration
  `finance_allocation_lab.0003_reconciliation_proposals` adds only proposal/history
  tables, constraints and an immutable-history trigger. Normal settings/migration
  graph exclude this app. No foundation/shared migration or access grant was
  added/applied. Existing staff/superuser/report/purchasing authority is not
  repurposed as Finance access.

## 2026-10-20 — Inventory/transfer register location-filter recovery

**Completed the bounded existing viewing workflow; no transfer-write feature or
new authority.** Tests first reproduced a real UI defect, not a new backend
disclosure: after refreshed scope removed the selected location, filter state
remained set to its ID but the HTML select visually fell back to **All permitted
locations**. The notice asked users to clear the filter without providing an
explicit clear control. Unrelated catalog failures also misrepresented the
retained filter as All. Existing report hooks already suppressed invalid-scope
requests and aborted/ignored obsolete responses; those safeguards are unchanged.

### Actual correction

`src/InventoryRegisters.tsx` keeps a disabled selected option identifying the
unavailable location (ID only, not cached protected location contents), with
linked live status explaining why no results are shown. Users can deliberately:
- **Clear unavailable location filter** to request the current explicitly
  selected BU's server-authorized report, reset to page one and retain dates;
- choose a **currently permitted location** to resume that narrower filter.

Neither occurs automatically. Pending/failed scope checks retain the exact
selection and dates, do not announce confirmed location removal, and do not
show cached report rows. No clear/reselect can grant a panel or data scope.
The error message now accurately says no data is **displayed until scope is
verified**, rather than implying no earlier requests ever occurred.

No report-hook, report API/service, calculation, export, write endpoint,
permission, grant definition, business rule or migration changed. Existing
field masking, fixed selected-BU scope, pagination and server enforcement remain.
No forms/drafts are remounted. Application changes cover the existing filter
control/status and a narrowly scoped mobile CSS adjustment that prevents the
controls clipping inside the card.

### What the real browser/backend actually proved

Both cases sign in as the existing disposable nonstaff persona, choose TVL,
open **Inventory & Warehouses → Inventory & transfer registers**, choose the
register and location, and load non-empty real data. Reused existing reporting
fixture helpers/capability definitions in the disposable database only; no shared
persona, grant or role is changed. The fixture's receipt/transfer facts are setup
data, not transfer actions exposed or submitted by the browser.

Remove the selected Location's TVL membership in the guarded fixture. Actual
explicit filtered GET becomes **403**, without rows. Refreshing report scope
produces the unavailable option/status, removes the table and makes **no new
old-location or unfiltered report request**. Native Enter on the clear button
then initiates a new BU-scoped GET; explicit reselect loads the still-permitted
location with unchanged dates. Cross-BU direct probing returns **403**.
Cost/value fields are absent in actual responses. Revoking panel assignment in
the isolated fixture makes direct reading **403** and clears the displayed table
after refresh; the client does not gain authority through its filter.

Whole-foundation snapshot/digest comparisons after fixture changes show reads,
denials, clear/reselect and refresh change no business/audit/payment/stock facts.
The new PostgreSQL check also preserves location membership through its reads.
Only real sign-in and existing selected-BU POSTs are allowed by the browser
proxy; no transaction/transfer POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE is submitted.
The native clear/refresh buttons use keyboard Enter; select choices use browser
DOM change events, **not claimed native select-key traversal**. Both viewports
passed card-control-boundary and page-overflow checks; screenshots/traces are ignored generated evidence
at `generated-artifacts/inventory-register-real-browser/`.

### Existing authorization semantics and limits

Location eligibility in the filter and a BU-wide report data grant are
**different facts**. Removing a current location membership invalidates an
explicit filter; it does not itself revoke a BU report grant or rewrite
historical inventory/transfer facts. An explicitly cleared filter requests a
**fresh** authorized BU report; fresh history may legitimately reference that
old location under the unchanged service contract. This is not reuse of the
removed filter's cached response. Narrower historical visibility must not be
invented as a new access rule in this UI repair. Never interpret the old row
cache, current dropdown options or UI-only masking as permission.

Out-of-order success/403/503 protection and transient scope failure recovery
are deferred rendered mocks, distinct from the actual authenticated native
scope-removal/clear/reselect/masking/revocation checks. No new native transient
network injection or whole-ERP/privileged-role browser rerun. Full frontend was
run (**333/333 passed before the final CSS-only narrow-layout adjustment; no
JavaScript, TypeScript or test source changed afterward**); full backend was not
repeated because backend behavior is unchanged and the relevant expanded API
module passed. No general screen-reader or production
security certification. No shared authenticated acceptance, data/grant/credential
changes, shared preview restart/seed, production connection, purchases, privacy
change or publishing. Temporary database, accounts and private credentials are
discarded by the verified guarded runner.

## 2026-10-20 — Warehouse-capacity access and refresh recovery

**Completed the bounded Inventory recovery workflow, not all Inventory/team
acceptance.** Tests first reproduced stale measurements after denied editing,
refresh-induced draft loss, out-of-order record restoration and stale completion
callbacks. Actual authenticated disposable browser acceptance also reproduced
the old view-loss case: the detail GET was **403**, but the old measurements
remained after the attempted save. Backend enforcement was already correct;
no successful unauthorized backend read/write was demonstrated.

### Demonstrated findings and narrowly scoped fixes

1. **Denied edit was not a read-access check.** The editor only displayed its
   PUT error and retained old editable measurements. Current PUT **403/404**
   now refreshes the existing independently authorized capacity list. A fresh
   list with **view-only** capability keeps actual stored measurements but
   removes edit controls; a list omitting a location removes that card and all
   its measurements/controls. A current list **403/404** clears protected cards.
   Losing EDIT alone is **not** inferred to remove VIEW: native fixtures retain
   an explicit existing VIEW assignment while revoking EDIT.
2. **Refresh cleared all records before its response.** This unmounted other
   location forms and lost unsaved drafts. Current cards now survive pending
   refreshes. Network/5xx reads keep the prior snapshot with explicit
   **“Previously loaded measurements”** guidance; ordinary 400/write-network/
   write-503 failures preserve authorized content and drafts without guessing
   read revocation. After an actual denied edit, save stays blocked until fresh
   authorized data confirms edit capability. **Refresh capacity access** retries
   only the GET, never the PUT.
3. **Ordinary list loading had no request owner.** Newest-request, mounted and
   presentation-context guards now prevent older success/error/finally handlers
   from restoring rows, replacing a newer error or clearing current loading.
   Switching to administration-only and back clears obsolete measurements
   before the first committed return render and requires fresh authorization.
   A removed location's late PUT acknowledgement cannot refresh another
   current list. Pending PUTs are not aborted or automatically repeated.
4. **Revocation refreshed metadata only.** Successful assignment revocation in
   the combined legacy/warehouse presentation now also refreshes independently
   assigned measurements. Governance's administration-only presentation still
   makes **no measurement GET** and administrators gain no implicit viewing
   authority. A tests-first regression failed before this one-line correction.
5. **A saved snapshot could erase newer edits.** Two additional tests reproduced
   typing after submission or during its refresh, followed by an older saved
   snapshot replacing the new draft. Local dirty/version tracking now preserves
   those edits; success feedback distinguishes an accepted submitted payload
   from newer unsaved edits. PUT bodies/calculations/transaction rules are
   unchanged.

Only `src/WarehouseCapacity.tsx` changes application behavior. No backend/model,
capacity permission definition, administrator assignment policy, stock,
reservation, costing, journal, finance or historical record rule changed.
Capacity remains **per explicitly assigned physical location, independent of
selected BU/stock grants**; switching brand must not incorrectly remove those
independent rights. No new app migration, shared assignment or demo seed.

## 2026-10-20 — Current quotation read-access revocation recovery

**Completed a demonstrated frontend defect, not a speculative disclosure
claim.** With the original build, the real authenticated disposable salesperson
loaded a quote, then the isolated fixture revoked existing access. Actual
quote GET returned **404**, the attempted collection returned **404**, and the
order-access check became denied; the old quote still rendered. The original
desktop native case failed waiting for that protected detail to disappear.
There was **no successful unauthorized backend read/write**, and no new cost
leak was demonstrated. The defect was retention of previously authorized UI
content after confirmed current access loss.

### Minimal correction and preserved boundaries

- `PurchasingTransactions` retains its existing order-access recheck after
  current-context 403/404 transaction denials and also asks the parent to
  revalidate the **currently displayed** quotation. The shared helper covers
  selected-quote actions and receipt/commitment/quote-creation denial paths;
  it does not retry POSTs, abort them or change their identity/outcome.
- `PurchasingWorkbench` reads the existing authoritative detail/preparation
  endpoint. Only a **current quote-read 403/404** removes the cached quotation,
  its document/details and quote-dependent controls, with the normal visible
  lookup error. An action denial alone is not proof of read-access loss.
- Successful read verification retains/refreshes the authorized response.
  Network/5xx failures retain the previously loaded snapshot and draft, with
  **“Quote access could not be rechecked”** status guidance to retry lookup.
  Editing/loading a new quote or changing BU clears obsolete guidance.
- Guards cover current BU, username, selected quote, explicit lookup/navigation,
  newest verification and unmount. An obsolete response cannot clear or restore
  another/currently reloaded quote. A pending explicit lookup is not cancelled
  by an old action denial.
- The transaction component is not remounted. Confirmed read loss intentionally
  removes quote-dependent form DOM; its local drafts and unacknowledged retry
  identities remain in the component. Rendered tests restore an allowed mocked
  lookup and prove the amount/key/payload survived. Action-only/transient
  cases retain the visible authorized quote and draft controls.

No backend service, API contract, grant/role definition, financial calculation,
historical snapshot, stock rule or permission was changed. No application
migration or shared-demo upgrade is needed.

lookup is still denied, and stock is also denied. BU switching clears old
context. Exactly one denied POST, no automatic retries, and the whole
foundation business digest is unchanged after the fixture revocation.

The independent action-only case lowers the existing disposable Manager
assignment to the existing Salesperson role: **no new assignment/grant/role**
is created. A **15%** approval is then genuinely denied while existing quote
reading remains allowed. One actual authorized GET acknowledgement is lost
only at the loopback test proxy (502), not fabricated by the backend. Quote
and approval-reason draft remain, with transient-verification guidance.
Explicit native lookup recovers via actual GET **200**, clears that guidance
and preserves the reason. An explicit identical API approval retry remains
**403**, with the same key/payload and no business/audit/idempotency writes.

Initial tests-first rendered run was **1 passed / 9 failed** (the three
additional sequencing/creation cases came later); original desktop native
read-loss test was **0/1**. Intermediate tests incorrectly expected
quote-dependent form DOM to remain after confirmed loss, or expected approval
to stay enabled. More importantly, removing the final approval role also
removed read access under the existing policy. Corrected the test fixture
to lower—not remove—that role and positively verify real allowed reads.
Legacy sequencing assertions now expect the two intentional read-only
authorization rechecks, not extra transaction retries. Final results above
are green; no policy was changed to satisfy a test.

revocation; retained data is explicitly identified as previously loaded.
The full backend suite was not rerun for this frontend-only correction; focused
backend and actual native evidence are distinguished above from the full
frontend run. Ordinary nonstaff read loss was checked at desktop/mobile;
action-grade downgrade/recovery was desktop. Deferred/out-of-order network

acknowledgement loss after an actual permitted backend response.

## 2026-10-20 — Owner-approved nonstaff quotation choices and bilingual presentation

### Implemented scope and requirement mapping

This batch reuses Retail/Purchasing multi-line quotation creation rather than
creating a second sales engine. Shared users, credentials, grants, prices,
transactions, Favorites and demo data were not changed; the shared development
workflow was not restarted. All mutation/upgrade/browser fixtures were in
independently verified disposable PostgreSQL **16.15** clusters.

| Approved requirement | Current implementation/evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Ordinary authorized nonstaff sales select existing items/customers | New GET-only `quotation-choices` API requires the existing active `create_order` BU grant, synthetic actor and current approval-role assignment. It returns only current approved QAR prices/item presentation, synthetic customer choices and the caller's own discount authority. Nonstaff entry no longer depends on full staff governance/directory reads. |
| Quantities without cost or inventory-history disclosure | Exact decimal-string **Unreserved quantity** uses `StockBalance` only with independent `read_stock`, selected BU/legal entity and explicit location membership. No reserved amount, cost/value, suppliers or history; unmatched/unauthorized quantities are unavailable, not zero. Snapshot is not a reservation or availability promise. |
| Fixed approved prices; own-grade discounts | Client price/item override fields are rejected; server captures approved prices. Ordinary nonstaff above-grade requests are denied before writes. Existing staff-mediated above-own-grade requests still require existing manager approval; staff status does not approve them. Existing 10/20/30/50 ceilings remain. |
| Sales cannot create items | Choices are read-only and no item/variant creation action is added. Direct nonexistent item-creation routes are denied/404; staff price/configuration endpoints remain denied to nonstaff. No administrator powers or item-maintenance workflow was added. |
| Multi-line calculation and atomic submission | Existing 1–40-line, single-kind quotation engine, decimal rounding, price snapshots, idempotency and rollback are reused. Two lines at 1.25×19.99 and 2.75×10.05 with 5.25% discount produce list 52.63, discount 2.77 and net **49.86 QAR** under existing rounding. Invalid later lines create no partial quote. |
| Item/customer/sales presentation | Optional item English/Arabic name, Arabic category/description and local image reference; customer Arabic name and EN/AR contact. New quotes retain an application-immutable presentation snapshot of item details, quantities/prices/discount/totals, client/contact, salesperson identity, BU/date and optional department/validity/display terms/delivery wording. Existing item description/category are preserved; no invented company metadata. |
| English/Arabic | Entry and client-presentation labels support EN/AR; supplied Arabic content has explicit RTL direction. Missing Arabic content/images are flagged. No real company translation, image or salesperson identity is fabricated. This does not translate the entire ERP interface. |
| Validity, terms and delivery | Explicit optional inputs, initially blank. Displayed payment/delivery text cannot alter actual payment plans, approvals, reservations or delivery controls. **Terms and Conditions await owner-supplied text**. No legal text, validity duration, payment wording or delivery promise is invented. |
| Confidential data, direct requests and exports | Original supplier/governance/history/report/export gates are unchanged. Focused API/native-browser denials exercise staff configuration/directory, price writes, gross margin/history and unauthorized Excel/Word export. No new quotation export or financial permission is introduced. |
| Context/drafts/retry | Existing BU/user ownership, deferred-response suppression, unsaved-work and exact request/key retry guards remain. Added rendered late-A choices versus denied-B coverage; full existing pending-action/retry tests pass. No new shared assignment or seed. |

### Focused frontend correction

Code inspection found that cross-section conditional rendering unmounted local
transaction state without a departure decision. Added presentation-only
`useWorkspaceNavigationSafety`: explicit confirmation before discarding edited
transaction/return/packing-preview local state, native unload warning, and a
clear pending-submission alert instead of navigating away. Sidebar, Favorites,
Overview/My Page and history/fragment changes use the same decision.
Same-workspace child changes remain unblocked and keep forms mounted.
Purchasing tracks network-in-flight count independently of context-visible
action indicators, so changing BU does not make a still-running request disappear
from departure protection. Return submissions expose their existing pending state.
No API, permission, policy, posting, payload, idempotency key or automatic-retry
behavior changed. The guard is conservative; it does not persist drafts/history
or add recovery after a browser crash, and is not a general dirty-state tracker
for every configuration/report-settings form.

Harness setup attempts initially failed because of real-login bootstrap/reload
timing, test selectors/status assumptions and a stock response-shape assertion;
these were corrected in the harness, not server behavior. An interrupted run
was lost during a workspace restart and is **not** counted as evidence.
Final results below supersede those unsuccessful attempts.

transaction engine. It exposes multi-line commitment creation, independent
ordered/received-to-date/remaining progress, successive selected-line receipts,
CSV/XLSX preparation and explicit mapping/review-to-local-draft, existing
receipt/landed-charge records and staff-only supplier references.

supplier target activates the existing counterparties register rather than
merely scrolling to receipt rows. Inline navigation uses the same existing
functions. The existing per-user Procurement Favorite opens this section; no
per-subpage Favorite storage, URL routes or permissions were invented.

returns and policy-administration forms. The general Purchasing Workbench,

capabilities and approval/configuration prerequisites, cost field allowlists,

## Reproduction

In Replit, use the configured `Start application` workflow (also defined in `.replit`). It starts PostgreSQL, applies migrations, seeds synthetic examples, starts Django, and serves the Vite preview on port 5000.

Outside Replit, install Python dependencies with `uv sync --locked` and frontend dependencies with `npm ci`. Copy `.env.example` to `.env` if local overrides are needed, then run `uv run bash scripts/dev.sh`. Required local PostgreSQL 16 tools are `initdb`, `pg_ctl`, `createdb`, and `psql`.

Seed command (the runner already executed this successfully):

```sh
APP_ENV=demo DB_NAME=tivoli_erp_demo DB_USER="${PGUSER:-$(id -un)}" DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT=55432 python manage.py seed_demo
```

Fictional accounts include `demo_tivoli`, `demo_roche`, `demo_natuzzi`, `demo_multi`, and the staff-only synthetic `demo_admin`. The report-fixture command does not set, reset, or print passwords. If an account requires password setup, use the existing private command; input is hidden and the value is not stored in source:

```sh
APP_ENV=demo DB_NAME=tivoli_erp_demo DB_USER="${PGUSER:-$(id -un)}" DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT=55432 python manage.py set_demo_password --username demo_roche
```

After the base synthetic seed, load the fictional report review dataset with the owner-controlled local-only command:

```sh
APP_ENV=demo DB_NAME=tivoli_erp_demo DB_USER="${PGUSER:-$(id -un)}" DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT=55432 python manage.py seed_demo_reports
```

To remove only that command's tagged reporting records, run the same command with `--reset`. It retains demo users/passwords, untagged manual report configuration, and append-only export audit records. It refuses non-demo environments and non-local/unrecognized databases. Re-running without `--reset` refreshes the same fixture keys; it does not create posted stock, deliveries, payments, or journal entries.

For an outside-Replit `uv` environment, prefix the management commands with `uv run`. For a separately managed PostgreSQL server, set `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_HOST`, and `DB_PORT` to that development database; do not put credentials in source.

Reproduce the automated checks with the development PostgreSQL instance running:

```sh
export APP_ENV=demo
export DB_NAME=tivoli_erp_demo
export DB_USER="${PGUSER:-$(id -un)}"
export DB_HOST=127.0.0.1
export DB_PORT=55432
python manage.py migrate
python manage.py seed_demo
python manage.py test -v 2
npm run typecheck
npm run build
uv lock --check
```

## Milestone 2 transaction-service increment — review results

This addition stays within the backend-service scope: it adds stock/accounting models and deterministic internal services, with no new API or broad UI. The complete details and test-only accounting assumptions are in `MILESTONE_2_TEST_ONLY_ASSUMPTIONS.md`. No publishing, purchases, privacy-setting changes, or real company data were used.

### Implementation

- Added append-only synthetic stock movements, stock-balance projections, reservations, same-business-unit/location transfers, idempotency records, QAR ledger accounts, and draft-to-posted journal entries.
- Receipt service allocates eligible landed charges by purchase value; delivery consumes reservations and records revenue/inventory relief. Service writes are atomic; same idempotency key and payload replays the stored result, while a changed payload is rejected.
- Added PostgreSQL constraints and triggers for QAR/demo-only records, movement sign rules, transfer-bucket consistency, immutable movements/transfers/completed requests/posted journals, completed idempotency requests, and balanced posted journals with same-entity accounts.
- Reservation and transfer concurrency tests use two worker threads and assert distinct PostgreSQL backend PIDs.
- The exact chair fixture is test-only: 10 × QAR 1,000, QAR 2,000 allocated landed charges, then delivery of 2 × QAR 2,000; expected inventory QAR 12,000, revenue QAR 4,000, COGS QAR 2,400, and remaining inventory QAR 9,600.

- PostgreSQL test command: `APP_ENV=demo DB_NAME=tivoli_erp_demo DB_USER=postgres DB_PASSWORD= DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT=55432 python manage.py test --verbosity 2`
- Exact final summary: `Ran 33 tests in 5.608s` / `OK` — **33 tests, 0 failures/errors**, PostgreSQL 16.15. Django created the test database, applied all migrations, then dropped the temporary database.
- `python manage.py check`: **Pass**, no system-check issues.
- `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run`: **Pass**, no model changes missing from migrations.
- Restarted the existing development workflow: **Pass**. Migrations `foundation.0002` and `foundation.0003` applied to the local development database; the existing synthetic seed remained at 1 company, 3 units, 3 brands, 6 items, 12 variants, 12 locations, and 12 read-only stock examples. Read-only counts confirmed **0** stock balances, movements, reservations, transfers, journal entries, and idempotency records in that development database; transaction fixtures ran only in the temporary PostgreSQL test database.
- Preview smoke check: **Pass**. The root page rendered the existing synthetic sign-in screen after restart; browser console had only Vite connection and React DevTools informational messages.

### Confirmed limitations and decisions still open

- All financial mappings and recognition rules are labeled `TEST_ONLY_NOT_TIVOLI_APPROVED`. They are not finance-approved and must not be applied to real records.
- The test fixture assumes no tax, a single cost layer, QAR, and revenue recognition at delivery. Partial delivery/transfer valuation prorates current aggregate balance value (a simple average-cost calculation); there is no cost-layer ledger or finance-approved FIFO/weighted-average policy.
- Test clearing accounts are placeholders. Finance must decide the chart of accounts, receipt/landed-charge posting semantics, eligible charge categories and allocation basis, tax/currency policy, inventory-cost method, revenue-recognition point, and legal-entity treatment.
- Reservations currently have no release/expiry/approval workflow. Stock corrections, reversal postings, transit stock, and cross-business-unit/entity transfers are not implemented.
- Transaction services are internal only, with no API or UI. The existing read-only Milestone 1 stock example remains separate from the transaction ledger.

## Milestone 3 — synthetic purchasing-to-delivery services

### Implemented

- Added PostgreSQL models and migration `foundation.0008_approvedsellingprice_businessunitroleassignment_and_more` for per-unit role assignments and work calendars, approved selling-price revisions, synthetic counterparties, purchase receipts and landed charges, quotes and price snapshots, approvals, holds, reservations, simulated payments, readiness/storage events, charges, and exceptions.
- Added deterministic service and session-authenticated API flows for synthetic import receipt, purchase-value landed allocation/rate, stock and special-order quotes, role-based discount approvals, short holds, simulated deposit/balance recording, reservations, readiness, delivery, storage accrual, and approved storage exceptions. API writes use idempotency keys and retain the existing session CSRF behavior.
- Approval roles can be assigned per business unit only to a synthetic user who already has that unit’s active `create_order` grant. Discounts use the selling-price revision captured on the quote; price revisions and quote commercial terms are immutable. No named users, roles, `create_order` grants, approved prices, counterparties, or value bands were added by demo seeding.
- The synthetic seed now creates a configurable Friday-closed work calendar (Saturday/Sunday working) and an empty storage-exception policy for each seeded business unit. The development database received migration `0008` and the repeatable synthetic seed; no real records or permissions were added.
- Special-order payment terms support explicit per-order approval for full payment or a 40%–70% downpayment. A 40% payment does not reserve stock; stock reservation requires at least 50% non-returnable simulated payment. Stock delivery requires full payment unless a BU GM/CEO records a reasoned 5%–10% post-handover exception.
- Existing Milestone 2 stock movements and posted QAR journals remain the stock/accounting path. Synthetic payment records do not call a payment provider. Receipt, quote, payment, journal, approval, storage-charge, and workflow audit records are append-only/immutable as appropriate.
- `MILESTONE_3_PURCHASING_TO_DELIVERY.md` documents the test-only assumptions and API/configuration gaps. The roadmap now reflects that this is a backend/API prototype, not a production workflow.

## Milestone 4 — reporting and controlled exports

### Implemented

- Added report panels for sales, best sellers/categories, costs/expenses, gross margin, budgets versus actuals, inventory, purchase history, and transfer history. Filters support daily/monthly/quarterly periods and authorized business-unit, location, or explicit legal-entity scope.
- Added independent synthetic `ReportPanelGrant` and `ReportDataGrant` records, synthetic role memberships, revocation, staff configuration, configurable synthetic budgets, and synthetic item category labels. Panel assignment never creates underlying report-data capability or operational `UserActionGrant`.
- Every report and export checks authentication, panel assignment, capability, row scope, and sensitive-field scope on the server. Direct unit requests cannot cross grants. Multiple individual business-unit grants require choosing a unit; consolidated-company reports require an explicit legal-entity grant. Sensitive purchase, landed-cost, expense, inventory-value, transfer-value, category, and gross-margin fields remain separately permissioned.

- Added controlled Excel (`.xlsx`) and Word (`.docx`) downloads using the exact authorized report rows and fields, with a synthetic test-only label and audit record for each successful export. Denied exports create no audit record. Report access is also enforced for the Favorites “Reports” destination.
- Added the Reports page and staff-only Reporting Governance area while retaining palette administration, business-unit themes, and personal Favorites/My Page. Authorized synthetic panel managers can assign/revoke panels for synthetic users or roles through a restricted control; it cannot create data grants. Full data-grant configuration remains staff-only.
- Added an owner-controlled `seed_demo_reports` fixture command and separate append-only report-only synthetic sales facts. It seeds daily/monthly/quarterly examples for TVL/RBB/NAT, nine explicitly fictional/configurable sales budget examples, a synthetic Managing Partner panel-manager role, and three BU-scoped sales roles. The fixture labels sample rows as fictional, never creates real sales or posted transaction records, and does not alter demo passwords.
- The Managing Partner role has only sales and budget data grants for TVL/RBB/NAT; each BU sales role has only its own BU's ordinary-sales capability. No supplier-cost, landed-cost, inventory-history/value, transfer, expense, category, or gross-margin capability is seeded. Panel assignment stays separate from data permissions.

The new transaction-backed `SalesReportLine` remains sourced from the synthetic delivery service; `DemoReportSalesFact` is a separate report-only fixture model excluded from operational sales.
- Updated `scripts/dev.sh` to select an installed PostgreSQL server binary matching an existing local `PG_VERSION`. This preserves the ignored local PostgreSQL data if Replit refreshes the runtime to a different major version.

## Milestone 5 — portability, backup/restore, and synthetic load baseline

### Implemented

- Added `PORTABILITY_BACKUP_AND_LOAD.md` with portable Linux/macOS development prerequisites and setup for Django, PostgreSQL, migrations, the React/TypeScript Vite app, and synthetic-only seeding. The local `scripts/dev.sh` runner supports operator-managed local PostgreSQL without bootstrapping/creating that database; `USE_BUNDLED_POSTGRES=0` selects it. The synthetic runner refuses remote PostgreSQL hosts. Passwords remain operator-supplied and `.env` remains ignored.
- Extracted the loopback-only local PostgreSQL bootstrap into `scripts/local_postgres.sh`. It checks the existing `PG_VERSION`, selects matching installed tools when available, and refuses to initialize a non-empty data directory that lacks a version marker.
- Added `scripts/backup_local_demo.sh`, `scripts/restore_local_demo.sh`, and `scripts/test_backup_restore.sh`. Backup is limited to local `APP_ENV=demo` database `tivoli_erp_demo` and an external-to-project destination. Bundles contain a PostgreSQL custom dump, row-count/migration manifest, SHA-256 checksums, and an optional media archive. Restore targets must be new `tivoli_erp_restore_*` databases; the clean-test wrapper drops only the temporary database it created.
- Added `snapshot_integrity` to compare exact table row counts, applied migrations, and PostgreSQL major version after restore. SHA-256 checks catch accidental archive/file corruption; they are not a signature or authenticity guarantee.
- Added optional `MEDIA_ROOT` configuration and media backup/restore support. Current models contain no `FileField`/`ImageField`, no upload endpoint exists, and the development database had no media files. The media tests use synthetic files and verify safe extraction without overwriting existing content.

It creates a fresh local PostgreSQL load-test database with at least 8,000 synthetic catalog items, variants, stock rows, report-only sales examples, and up to 40 fictional session users. Each benchmark user has only TVL `read_stock` and sales-report scope; cross-unit stock and report requests are checked for denial. The load database is dropped by default.

## Synthetic-load pagination and query optimization — review update

This follow-up addresses the measured synthetic 8,000-item / 40-worker stock and sales-report slowdown. It changes neither underlying business permissions nor accounting/report meaning. The complete methodology and per-request instrumentation are in `PORTABILITY_BACKUP_AND_LOAD.md`; all performance data remains synthetic and the temporary load database is dropped after the run.

### Implementation

- Added per-request SQL count and duration capture, split timings for database fetch, Python transformation/aggregation, and JSON rendering, plus PostgreSQL `EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS, FORMAT JSON)` plans for stock pages, catalog lookup, report pages, line/fact queries, and the period aggregate.
- Stock and report APIs now accept `page`/`page_size` and return `total_count`, page count, and previous/next metadata. Default page size is 50, maximum 100. Stock order remains item code, SKU, and record ID; sales order is timestamp, source flag, and source ID. The authenticated UI has page-size selection and disabled/enabled previous/next controls with live page status.
- Business-unit and location authorization/filtering is applied before stock counting and slicing. Report data and field permissions, selected unit/location scope, and panel access are checked before paginating. Ordinary sales rows contain only selling price, quantity, description, item ID, warehouse location, and brand; no cost or margin fields are fetched for that panel. Best-seller/category aggregates run only for authorized requests to those panels.
- Reworked stock substring matching to produce candidate item/variant/location IDs before intersecting with the already-authorized stock queryset. It preserves matches across item code, description, brand, SKU, and location name. Removed stock `.distinct()` only after confirming the authorized location/business-unit join is unique by schema; deterministic ordering remains.
- Inclusive report dates now use configured-timezone-aware half-open timestamp bounds. Verified the synthetic Asia/Qatar day against the existing composite business-unit/time indexes. Sales exports continue to request the full authorized report independently of screen pagination and preserve their audit records.
- Added regression coverage for scoped stock page/location/search filtering, all five search fields, invalid page parameters, ordinary-sales row-field allowlisting, exact decimal-safe aggregates, local date boundaries, skipping unrelated sensitive aggregates, generic report paging, and complete Excel/Word exports while the screen is on one page.

### Verification

- Full PostgreSQL command: `APP_ENV=demo DB_NAME=tivoli_erp_demo DB_USER="${PGUSER:-$(id -un)}" DB_HOST=127.0.0.1 DB_PORT=55432 python manage.py test foundation --verbosity 1`
- Exact result: `Found 107 test(s)`; `Ran 107 tests in 33.047s` / `OK` — **107 tests, 0 failures/errors**, PostgreSQL 16.15. Django created, migrated, and dropped the temporary test database. `python manage.py makemigrations --check --dry-run` reported `No changes detected`; Django system checks were clean.
- `npm run typecheck`: **Pass** (`tsc --noEmit`). `npm run build`: **Pass**; Vite transformed 19 modules and built in **662 ms** (JS 286.06 kB, CSS 38.92 kB). `npm run test:contrast`: **Pass**, all 13 assertions.
- Final same-parameter load run: **8,000** catalog items, stock rows, and report-only sales facts; **40** synthetic users; **40** worker threads; **one** measured request/user/endpoint and **one** warm-up. Each endpoint had 40 measured requests. Cross-unit stock and report denials returned 403 as expected.

| Request | Instrumented pre-change p50 / p95 | Optimized p50 / p95 | Mean response bytes, pre → optimized |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Catalog lookup | 988.444 / 1,467.807 ms | 475.928 / 1,270.012 ms | 346 → 467 |
| TVL stock list | 35,984.476 / 42,308.071 ms | 704.342 / 1,058.293 ms | 2,760,173 → 17,274 |
| TVL sales report | 64,765.609 / 85,094.435 ms | 1,040.336 / 1,459.721 ms | 1,873,051 → 10,688 |

- Final SQL count/request: catalog **7** (pre **6**), stock **7** (pre **6**), sales report **13** (pre **11**); additional statements support exact pagination counts and grouped sales totals. Final per-request SQL-duration p50/p95: catalog **365.256 / 969.649 ms**, stock **591.909 / 887.858 ms**, sales report **861.123 / 1,357.945 ms**.
- Final per-request stage p50s, in catalog/stock/report order: database fetch **186.408 / 252.990 / 269.380 ms**; Python transformation/aggregation **0.540 / 2.576 / 0.154 ms**; JSON rendering **0.047 / 0.181 / 0.169 ms**.
- Final measured batch elapsed **3,005.558 ms**; Python CPU **2.613 seconds**; peak process RSS **93,348 KiB**; PostgreSQL counter delta **5,766,048 buffer hits, 0 reads, 0 temporary bytes**. The activity sampler saw up to **8 active PostgreSQL backends** in this short final run, although 40 worker threads were configured; the sampler maximum varied between these short runs and does not prove 40 simultaneous active SQL statements.
- Plan review: stock page no longer has the wide `Unique`/full-row sort; its deterministic order uses top-N sorting. Catalog lookup's final plan intersects candidate-ID subqueries with the authorized stock set, touching about **330** shared buffers for the benchmark term instead of joining all 8,004 stock rows before filtering (about **80,147** shared buffers in the old plan). The sales date bounds appear as timestamp index conditions on `demo_sales_unit_time_idx`; the line query uses `sales_report_unit_time_idx`. Plans and exact statements/timings are in ignored `generated-artifacts/synthetic-load-optimized-final.json`.
- Workflow restart and root preview check: **Pass**; Vite and Django started, migrations were current, system checks were clean, and the sign-in page rendered. A signed-in visual screenshot was not possible because the preview capture browser cannot authenticate; signed-in page behavior is covered by PostgreSQL-backed API tests and the frontend typecheck/build.

### Remaining limits

- The final short run's 40-thread configuration is not a long soak, stable capacity estimate, or proof of 40 simultaneously active database statements. Its eight-backend sampler maximum varied across runs. It excludes browser, TCP/TLS, Replit proxy, and external-hosting overhead; no lock-wait instrumentation was added.
- Catalog `icontains` still scans item and variant values without a trigram extension. The plan is materially narrower after candidate-ID filtering, but this remains a potential cost as catalogs grow.
- Exact report totals/counts still require database work across all 8,000 sample facts; report row transformation and returned page are limited to 50. Full authorized exports intentionally remain unpaginated and are functionally tested, but their time and memory were not load-tested.
- The older 247-second unpaginated benchmark in `PORTABILITY_BACKUP_AND_LOAD.md` is a historical run with a different instrumentation state. Use the instrumented pre-change and final run above for this comparison. None of these results establish an SLA or company daily transaction volume.
- No production database, real company records, Replit publishing, or project privacy settings were used or changed.

## Purchasing workbench — authorized read-side completion (2026-10-17)

### Implemented

- Added paginated, deterministic GET list/detail reads for synthetic receipts and landed-charge details, quotes, storage charges and exceptions, quote reservations, delivered sales lines, and counterparties.
- Authorization reuses existing server-side controls:
  - Quotes and storage charges require the active synthetic `create_order` grant and the existing active business-unit role assignment. Quote details also accept the selected-unit context so a stale or mismatched UI selection cannot imply access.
  - Receipt register/detail require the purchase-history report panel and data capability. Supplier unit cost and purchase value appear only with `SUPPLIER_COST`; charge/landed allocation fields only with `LANDED_COST`; receipt landed rate and inventory total require both. Cost masks are applied per authorized business unit before serialization.
  - Reservations require the inventory report panel and `INVENTORY` capability. The query scopes both quote and stock-balance business units and returns no stock value or cost fields.
  - Delivery lines require the sales report panel and `SALES` capability. The returned sale fields are selling price, quantity, description, item ID, warehouse location, and brand, with delivery ID/date metadata; revenue, COGS, customer IDs, and margin are omitted.
  - Counterparty list/detail reuse the existing staff-only synthetic governance access. `SyntheticCounterparty` has no business-unit relationship, so this remains a global synthetic staff directory, not a per-unit directory.
- Report-backed receipts, reservations, and deliveries apply the existing BU/location/date filters before pagination. API lists use the existing paging limit (default 50, maximum 100); the workbench requests 20 rows per page.
- Added read-only workbench sections for receipts/landed charges, quote/order lists and details, storage charges, reservations, deliveries, and staff-only counterparties. Each section has loading, empty, denied, error, detail, and previous/next states. Only GET requests were added; no transaction or configuration write controls were introduced.
- The prior staff configuration readiness and quote-ID lookup remain. The quote lookup now includes its selected BU. Existing Reports, Favorites, controlled Excel/Word exports, transaction rules, seeded demo values, grants, prices, counterparties, and passwords were not changed.

## Personal reporting workspace — completed synthetic increment (2026-10-17)

### Implemented behavior and boundaries

- Added owner-only persisted named report views. Users can create, rename/update, delete, select and reorder their assigned panels with accessible Move up/Move down controls. Views retain period, explicit BU or company scope, location, dates, page and page size. The existing ad-hoc report controls can supply the draft filters; loading a saved view uses its own retained filters, not another view's or the current ad-hoc scope.
- Persistence contains only owner, name, ordered panel codes, allowlisted filters and metadata. Unknown fields (including report rows or user overrides), unassigned/unknown/duplicate panels and malformed filters are rejected. Names are unique per owner. Staff cannot read, update or delete somebody else's preferences. Migration `0012_personal_report_views` adds the preferences table without changing existing records.
- Saving assigned-panel presentation preferences does **not** certify data access. A saved filter may subsequently be unavailable or point outside granted scope; it never grants authority. On each saved-view load, the server reuses the existing `build_report` authorization path for every panel using a one-row query and discards the report result. It returns only availability/reason metadata, never report facts. Missing/revoked panel, data, role membership, BU/company or location access yields an unavailable state, with no automatic scope substitution.
- Each displayed panel fetches the existing reporting API afresh, preserving its current row/field authorization, ordinary-sales field allowlist and optional sensitive-field masking. Ordered panels show authorized rows, summaries and returned trend/best-seller/category/expense breakdowns, with explicit page navigation. Existing Excel/Word handlers still build/export the full current authorized result and audit successful exports.
- Previous panel data is cleared during view revalidation, request/filter changes, failures and export denial. Aborted or out-of-order responses cannot restore an old view or scope. Report/preference fetches use `cache: "no-store"`; catalog, report and saved-view responses carry private/no-store cache headers. Focus, returning to the tab and manual reload trigger fresh checks. No report results or permissions are stored in preferences or browser storage.
- Existing report-panel-manager/staff assignment capabilities remain separate and unchanged. No new shared users, roles, grants, approval assignments, approved prices, report facts or budgets were seeded by this increment. No accounting/payment/company policies were changed.
- Changed implementation files: `foundation/models.py`, `foundation/migrations/0012_personal_report_views.py`, `foundation/personal_reporting.py`, `foundation/urls.py`, `foundation/reporting_views.py`, `src/PersonalReportingWorkspace.tsx`, `src/personal-reporting-workspace.css`, `src/ReportingArea.tsx`, `src/reporting-api.ts`. ## Catalog/stock/monthly-sales responsiveness — verified isolated comparison

### Concurrency findings and scope

- The old harness ran unsynchronized mixed endpoint loops. Its 25 ms Python-thread PostgreSQL sampler counted active SQL, not overlapping authenticated requests, and could miss short queries or be delayed by Python scheduling. The historical 6.9/5.6/5.2-second p95s were not reproducible with the new synchronized baseline **before any application query change**; do not attribute that historical difference to the application optimization.
- The harness now schedules bounded per-endpoint waves with a barrier, batching safely when sessions exceed workers. It records actual peak in-flight requests, per-request monotonic start/end, thread ID and response SHA-256. All three endpoints reached **40 overlapping requests in every before/after run**. Broken barriers are bounded and failures do not become successful samples.
- An independent process sampled `pg_stat_activity` every 10 ms. Its maxima were **36 active backends before / 22 after**, excluding itself but including the in-process diagnostic sampler. The original in-process sampler reported **28/35 before and 12/4 after**. Neither number is request concurrency or simultaneous CPU execution; requests also wait between statements in Python/session/auth/rendering work. The independent sampler also saw up to **42 idle ClientRead backends**. No lock-contention cause was established.
- All workloads used a separate temporary **PostgreSQL 16.15** cluster on loopback port **55439**, not the shared preview database/server. Limits: **64 connections**, **64 MiB shared buffers**, **4 MiB work memory**, **15-second statement timeout**, **90-second per-command cutoff**; environment **8 GiB memory / four CPU-equivalents**.
- Dataset: **8,000 generated catalog items, variants, stock rows and report-only sales facts**, plus the small standard synthetic seed. **40 session-cookie clients**, ordinary TVL stock/sales data scope, no benchmark-user write grants. No real users, records or access assignments were used.

### Targeted implementation

- Stock: determine page IDs using the original authorized, ordered, filtered query before hydrating wide related display fields. Both inner and outer queries retain the existing scope and deterministic item-code/SKU/PK order. Small results, including the one-row catalog search, retain the original slice path.
- Sales: bound each ordered source of the `UNION ALL` to the required page window before merging. Global timestamp/source/PK order, duplicates, decimal totals, date filters, exact counts, full-period trends and masking remain unchanged. Unpaged exports retain the original full authorized query.
- No indexes/migrations, authorization/grant changes, permission caches, rendering changes, accounting rules or business transitions were introduced. Catalog `icontains` matching remains unchanged: its roughly 5–6 ms isolated query plan did not justify a new search behavior or extension.
- Benchmark EXPLAIN uses the same page builders as the API. Added `--reuse-fixture` to the existing guarded management command so before/after runs can use the identical disposable fixture; requested item/variant/stock/fact/session counts are checked and the fixture is not reseeded.

### Equivalent before/after evidence

Two repetitions per phase on the **same fixture and PostgreSQL instance**, each using one warm-up per endpoint and one measured request per client/endpoint. The same updated concurrency harness, SQL logging and diagnostics were used for both phases. The only intervening application changes were the bounded query builders above. Metrics below pool **80 requests per endpoint per phase** using the harness's interpolated percentiles.

| Endpoint | Before p50 / p95 (ms) | After p50 / p95 (ms) | SQL/request, unchanged | Mean response bytes, unchanged |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Catalog lookup | 483.793 / 594.103 | 490.972 / 570.099 | 7 | 467 |

## Overview business-unit switching — race/failure regression completion

### Tests first and smallest frontend correction

- Added four rendered App tests to `scripts/overview-location-tree-ui.test.tsx`. The initial `npm run test:overview-ui` run reported **9 tests: 6 passed, 3 failed, 0 cancelled/skipped**, reproducing a delayed organization snapshot overwriting the newer context, session-selection POSTs applying out of order, and a successful selection followed by a failed organization refresh leaving the old context visible. The explicit 403-denial case already passed.
- `src/App.tsx` now queues each existing selection POST together with its organization/Favorites refresh. Rapid requests are processed in submission order, rather than allowing a late session mutation or scoped snapshot to overwrite a later one. A response-ID-only fix would not prevent out-of-order server session changes.
- The current confirmed unit label, palette and tree remain together until another authorized organization snapshot is returned; an accessible status announces `Updating business-unit context…`. Sign-out is disabled while this queue is active so it does not overlap those session mutations.
- A denied selection retains the confirmed context and displays the original server error. A subsequent successful selection clears that error.
- If selection succeeds but organization refresh fails, the UI clears organization/stock/Favorites context and hides scoped module content. It shows a disabled `Business unit` selector with `Business-unit context unavailable`, uses the existing neutral slate palette, preserves the server error, and provides `Reload business-unit context`. Recovery reads the actual existing session context; it does not replay the selection POST.
- Valid-context labels, unit palette assignments, location labels/hierarchy/order/indentation and the real API contracts are unchanged. No server implementation, models, migration, grants, payment/accounting rules, demo seed or production configuration changed.

3. `a 403-denied unit switch preserves the confirmed label theme and tree and shows the server error`
4. `successful selection followed by failed organization refresh clears stale context and can safely reload`

The first two tests deliberately release later responses first when the implementation permits overlap (the original failing path); with the fix they verify that the next selection cannot start before the preceding refresh completes. Assertions cover selected-unit control, heading, palette, exact location labels, final synthetic server session, pending status, error recovery, and no extra selection mutation during read-only reload. The existing five list/hierarchy/empty/switching tests remain. All HTTP in these frontend tests is synthetic and mocked; no shared API data is written.

## Stock-view stale response protection — complete

### Tests first and bounded frontend change

- Added `scripts/stock-context-ui.test.tsx`, rendering the actual App with synthetic mocked HTTP, deferred stock responses, distinct A/B rows and counts (103/61), and real pagination controls. `package.json` adds `npm run test:stock-ui` to the complete frontend suite.

The test assertions were changed to compare alert text rather than whole DOM objects, and deferred responses are settled during teardown. This keeps failure diagnostics bounded without weakening their assertions. No application change preceded the completed red baseline.
- Only `src/App.tsx` application behavior changed. Stock reads now carry a request identity and confirmed unit context; only the current request may update rows, totals/pagination, errors or loading state. Context replacement/invalidation and successful logout invalidate outstanding reads; unmount cleanup also invalidates them. Requests for an unverified/stale context do not start.
- Stock error handling is centralized inside the guarded request, replacing unguarded caller catches. A current error, including 403, clears the prior stock page and displays the original server error. Obsolete success/error/finally paths have no effect. A search retry still trims the search term, resets to page 1 and uses the existing API query parameters.
- No API, backend/model/migration, grants, search matching, response ordering, pagination contract, selected-unit queue, palette mapping or company-policy changes. The existing unit-selection CSRF handling and server permission checks remain authoritative. No CSS or dependencies changed.

Assertions include exact row order, server-returned counts and page metadata, previous/next availability, loading status/search disablement, selected-unit/theme consistency, no stale alerts, safe GET-only recovery without another selection POST, and the scoped/trimmed search retry. ## Stock-error recovery after same-BU refresh — complete

### Tests-first findings and narrow frontend correction

- Before changing application code, `npm run test:stock-ui` reported **15 tests: 12 passed / 3 failed**, **7,434.873825 ms**. The new tests reproduced an obsolete stock error remaining after successful same-BU recovery, and an unrelated sign-out error disappearing on stock search retry. The current-403 test already passed.
- `src/App.tsx` now keeps `stockError` separate from the existing general error. Only a current stock response can set or resolve its stock error; successful stock reads no longer need to clear a general alert. Existing context invalidation clears stock rows/loading/error together. Search and page-size retries clear only the stock error, not unrelated alerts.
- Stock alerts retain the existing alert styling and `role="alert"`. A current stock 403 and an unrelated sign-out failure can coexist, and resolving/retrying stock leaves the sign-out alert intact. Stale successes cannot erase a current denial; stale failures cannot reintroduce one.
- BU/location scope, API paths and query parameters, search trimming, ordering, pagination, same-BU reload trigger, palette behavior, request-generation guards and server authorization are unchanged. No backend, model, migration, CSS or dependency changes.
- All palette/auth/stock interactions in the new rendered tests are synthetic mocked HTTP. The failed sign-out is simulated, not a live account/session mutation. No shared data or credentials were used or changed.

### Exact new rendered tests — all 4 passed

1. `successful same-BU refresh removes a resolved stock error and restores the fresh page`
2. `an obsolete failure cannot restore a stock error after same-BU recovery`

## Purchasing transaction completion context and retry hardening — complete

### Tests first; reproduced failures

- Added `scripts/purchasing-transaction-context-ui.test.tsx`, rendering the actual staff `PurchasingWorkbench` with fictional GET configuration/counterparty/quote fixtures and deferred, in-memory POST responses. No browser request reaches a server. The fixture rejects any abort signal on a POST.
- After correcting test selectors (staff governance and transaction access chips are distinct), the final pre-fix focused run reported **14 tests: 1 passed / 13 failed**, **5,361.650548 ms**, exit **1**. Unchanged lost-response retry behavior already passed. Actual defects included A quote **101** replacing B quote **202**, A feedback/errors affecting B, stale A access rechecks, unnecessary register refreshes, lost/incorrect busy ownership, and action-name-only keys reused for changed requests.
- No live duplicate transaction was submitted or claimed. Backend duplicate protection is independently verified by the isolated existing PostgreSQL tests below.

### Minimal application scope

- Application edits are limited to `src/PurchasingTransactions.tsx`. A per-user/BU context identity invalidates stale completion callbacks across BU switches, including A→B→A, and unmount. It clears context-specific feedback/error/busy state without resetting transaction drafts or remounting forms.
- All three submission paths—generic quote actions, receipt creation, and quote creation—still await the same POST endpoints with unchanged payloads, CSRF headers and same-origin credentials. Only current-context completions update feedback/errors or invoke parent refresh/quote-opening callbacks. Access rechecks also verify their originating context. Busy completion checks ownership, so an older action cannot clear a newer action's indicator.
- POSTs are **not aborted**, automatically retried, cancelled or rolled back by navigation. The tests explicitly settle them after switching and verify no automatic second POST.
- Retry keys are associated with the exact request identity (user, BU, action, endpoint and payload), not just action name. Exact unacknowledged retries keep the same key/body; different BU, quote/endpoint or payload uses a distinct key. Returning to a prior unchanged request retains its original key.
- A stale/unseen success retains its key so a subsequent identical retry can replay the original server result instead of creating a new transaction. Only an acknowledged current-context success retires that identity's key. The next deliberate submission after acknowledged success receives a new key, as before. Backend idempotency, authorization and transaction/payment policies are untouched.
- Updated the existing source-contract assertion for the new key binding, and added `test:purchasing-transaction-ui` to `test:purchasing-ui`.

## Synthetic purchase commitments and partial receipts — 2026-10-18

### Implemented

## Multi-line synthetic commitment and receipt workbench — 2026-10-18

## Synthetic readiness/storage notification outbox — 2026-10-18

### Implemented

- Added `NotificationOutboxIntent`, uniquely linked one-to-one to an existing `WorkflowEvent`. Database constraints keep records synthetic, limit states to pending/retry/dry-run-recorded/dry-run-failed, and cap dry-run attempts at three.
- Readiness and storage-charge notification intents are inserted in the same atomic transaction as their existing quote/storage state change and append-only workflow event. Existing idempotency replay returns the original result and does not create another event or intent. Storage-exception events are not notification intents.
- The intent contains no recipient, channel, or message body. The dry-run worker derives only the intent ID, workflow-event ID/kind, quote ID, and an explicit dry-run/no-external-send label.
- Added `process_notification_outbox_dry_run`, a local synthetic-demo PostgreSQL management command. It runs only outside an atomic block, uses a fixed in-memory fake sink, rejects other sink types, serializes each claim with a PostgreSQL row lock, processes each intent at most once per invocation, and records only a generic failure code. The final state is `dry_run_recorded`, never delivered; no email, WhatsApp, SMS, or network adapter exists.
- No UI/API endpoint was added because this is an internal test-only worker. Existing authorization, notification timing, storage calculations, event wording, payment behavior, and permissions were not changed.

## Synthetic location-scoped warehouse capacity foundation — 2026-10-18

### Implemented

- Added an explicit `LocationCapacity` profile for physical locations. A location is treated as capacity-managed only when an ERP/system administrator explicitly creates the profile; the existing location hierarchy is not used to infer physical-vs-logical location type. Unconfigured profiles store no fabricated zero values.
- Capacity records store separate decimal-string measures: total floor area (`m²`), allocated storage floor area (`m²`), and received-goods volume (`m³`). Available floor area is derived as total minus allocated. No `m²`/`m³` conversion or total volumetric capacity is inferred. The storage precision is six decimal places.
- Added independent per-location `view_capacity` and `edit_capacity` grants. Edit includes view. Assignments are separate from `read_stock`, `create_order`, report capabilities, and purchasing approval roles. The assignment UI/API requires a Django superuser in `APP_ENV=demo`; `is_staff` alone is insufficient. Targets must be active synthetic demo accounts.
- Managers must have an explicit assignment for each configured physical location. Every capacity-list/detail read and capacity write rechecks the active location grant server-side; direct access to an unassigned location is denied. Capacity-only demo users can sign in and receive only the organization/location context associated with their capacity assignment; this context does not permit the stock API.

The broader architecture still calls for partial delivery/returns and credits, late landed cost after sale, closed-period controls and correction/reversal proofs.
