Existing empty configuration is not a missing grant to be invented. These dependencies do not block the independent quantity-integrity diagnostic below.

### New independent implementation

- Added operator-only `python manage.py reconcile_stock_quantities`, reusing the existing local synthetic PostgreSQL integrity-snapshot guard unchanged. There is no HTTP endpoint, application permission, user assignment, seed change, schedule, network operation or repair mode.
- Compares stored on-hand quantity with movement quantity sums, and stored reserved quantity with active reservation sums. Uses exact decimals, stable bucket/field ordering and separately grouped queries to avoid join multiplication; zero-quantity landed charges do not increase stock, and `StockExample` is never read.
- Establishes a standalone PostgreSQL `REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY` snapshot so concurrent committed transfers cannot create a false mixed-generation discrepancy. Nested caller transactions are rejected rather than silently using weaker isolation.
- Emits JSON statuses `empty`, `consistent` or `mismatch`, bucket counts and exact quantity discrepancies. A mismatch gives a failing command result, with no repair. No cost/value, identities or capacity contents are emitted.
- Added `STOCK_QUANTITY_RECONCILIATION.md`. Remaining independent integrity slices are transfer-pair structure and posted-journal balance verification against existing test-only invariants, without adding financial mappings or app-user access.

## Synthetic packing-list receipt preparation — 2026-10-18

### Inspection and completed scope

The roadmap/current implementation already contained the scoped purchasing-to-delivery transaction workbench, multi-line commitment/partial receipt flow, ledger-backed Inventory, post-delivery balance/idempotency behavior, capacity audit register and Reporting/Dashboards/controlled exports. They were preserved, not reimplemented. The existing CSV/XLSX supplier preview was browser-local and code-match-only: it had no exact variant selection or reviewed receipt-draft handoff. This increment completes that bounded next stage.

- Extended the existing preview inside **Purchasing → Receive imported goods → Prepare a receipt from a synthetic packing list**. Original Inventory preview behavior is unchanged when preparation is not requested.
- Each line requires an explicit authorized variant choice, an existing receiving location, a separately entered positive receipt quantity (at most two decimal places), and human source-unit review. Ambiguous, unmatched, invalid, pending or denied rows block the whole draft; even one candidate is not auto-selected.
- Warehouse m³ enrichment remains local and separate from source m²/m³. No unit conversion, base unit, location type, supplier template or barcode format is assumed.
- Review only copies lines into the existing receipt draft. Synthetic supplier and QAR costs must still be entered/reviewed, followed by an explicit **Record synthetic receipt** action through the existing API. Source edits/mapping/enrichment/choice changes invalidate copied lines. No upload or unconfirmed preview creates stock, reservation, cost, accounting, receipt, commitment, capacity or audit records.
- The existing final POST receives only its supported `business_unit_id`, `supplier_id`, `lines` and `charges`; source files/references/units/measurements are not persisted. Unchanged explicit retries retain the exact payload and idempotency key; successful completion clears the copied draft.
- Added GET-only `/api/stock-receipt-candidates/`, reusing the existing active `read_stock`/selected-BU/legal-entity/location-membership ledger scope. Exactly six display fields are returned: `variant_id`, `variant_sku`, `variant_description`, `item_code`, `item_description`, `brand_name`. No costs, quantities, suppliers, movements or capacity contents are returned. Variants are deduplicated across location buckets and ordered by SKU/ID. Input and result limits fail explicitly rather than truncating ambiguous matches.
- Local files remain entirely browser-side; only codes/unit go to the scoped GET lookups. No storage service, network transport, package/dependency or migration was added. No grants, roles, users, prices, counterparties, approver assignments, transaction services or business policies changed.
- Added `PACKING_LIST_RECEIPT_PREPARATION.md`; updated Milestone 3 and roadmap scope.

## Explicit purchase-commitment packing-list receipt preparation — 2026-10-18

### Completed workflow and preserved boundaries

- Inspected the current roadmap/spec, previous preparation handoff, existing purchase-commitment progress/receipt views, receiving services, permission checks and regression harness before editing. Multi-line commitments, partial receiving, row locks, over-receipt rejection, landed allocation, rollback and idempotency already existed; none was reimplemented or changed.
- In **Purchasing → Transaction workbench → Receive imported goods → Prepare a receipt from a synthetic packing list**, users can choose **Existing purchase commitment**, explicitly choose an existing authorized commitment, and map each source row to an exact line within that commitment. No commitment/line/supplier/item match or unit conversion is inferred. Even one available commitment or line is not automatically selected.
- Reuses the existing paginated `/api/purchasing/commitments/` progress already loaded by the workbench. Ordered, received-to-date and remaining quantities remain visible. Commitment mode does not use the ledger-candidate endpoint to determine choices or broaden catalog access; it references only variants already disclosed by the existing authorized commitment document.
- Each source row retains its source code, description, quantity, unit and optional reference. A separately entered confirmed receipt quantity, existing authorized location and explicit quantity/unit acknowledgement are required. Missing/invalid/stale/denied/ambiguous mappings, duplicate use of one commitment line, and quantities above remaining block the whole draft. Quantities are compared with exact decimal arithmetic, not floating-point rounding.
- Review copies local lines only. The copied draft fixes the supplier from the explicitly chosen commitment and carries exact commitment/line/variant/location IDs and confirmed quantities. Committed unit values are neither displayed nor entered. Existing direct receiving remains available as an explicit separate mode, with its existing cost inputs and ledger-only matching scope.
- Only the existing **Record synthetic receipt** submits a POST. Its supported payload contains `business_unit_id`, `supplier_id`, `purchase_commitment_id`, `lines` and `charges`; commitment lines carry `commitment_line_id`, `variant_id`, `location_id` and `quantity`, without `unit_cost` or source-file/unit/measurement metadata. The existing server revalidates current remaining quantities, scope and document links and uses immutable committed values for the unchanged landed-cost allocation/posting path.
- Editing source/mode/commitment/line/quantity/location/review invalidates copied lines. Progress changes reset preparation review; BU/user/staff/refresh ownership and A→B→A invalidation remain in place. Delayed direct-item lookup results cannot replace a selected commitment mapping. The portless development domain returned 502; that was a different URL, not evidence that the configured preview failed. Scheme and port were preserved; no broad CSRF trust was added.

Authenticated live-browser UI was **not** verified; no credentials were accessed/reset and no transaction was submitted. ## 2026-10-18 — Read-only synthetic posted-journal balance verification

### Implemented scope

- Added `foundation/journal_verification.py` and the operator-only `python manage.py verify_posted_journal_balances` command. Operator documentation: `POSTED_JOURNAL_BALANCE_VERIFICATION.md`.

An imbalance includes exact decimal-string debit/credit totals and difference; other discrepancies include internal IDs/reference or currency facts and line counts. A mismatch prints JSON and raises `CommandError`. No output file, posting, repair, grant, audit event, HTTP endpoint, application panel or schedule is created.
- Existing models, migrations, account mappings, transaction services, authorization, report masking/exports and production configuration are unchanged. Monetary discrepancies are sensitive shell/database-operator output, not a new ordinary-user reporting permission.
- Roadmap marks the diagnostic complete. Stock quantity and transfer-pair diagnostics remain separate and unchanged. Deferred sidebar navigation remains unimplemented.

- **No writes:** unchanged full entry/line/account/idempotency facts and whole-schema table-count manifest; captured diagnostic SQL contains no DML/DDL; unrelated descriptive/payload/account-class fields are not selected. An injected accidental `UPDATE` fails with PostgreSQL SQLSTATE **25006** (read-only transaction), rather than relying on the immutability trigger to stop it.
- **Consistency:** a writer with a different real PostgreSQL backend PID commits a balanced journal between header and line reads. The current snapshot sees **one entry/two lines**; the next sees **two/four**, both consistent.
- **Precision/no cancellation:** independent copied imbalances of +10.00 and -10.00 remain two discrepancies rather than netting away. Four maximum-size stored amount lines remain exact even with a caller Decimal precision of 6; the copied imbalance yields debit **199999999999999.98**, credit **199999999999999.97**, difference **0.01**.
- **No protection bypass:** unbalanced/empty/single-line posting, committed drafts, foreign-entity/non-QAR references and posted mutations are rejected by existing PostgreSQL protections. Unpersistable imbalance cases use in-memory copies only. The persisted discrepancy changes mutable account metadata only in an isolated fixture; repeated command reads report the same reference error and never repair it.

## Synthetic non-posting sales-return intake and inspection — 2026-10-19

### Implemented scope

Added a return-intake register and draft/inspection forms under the existing **Purchasing Workbench → Sales-return intake — synthetic, non-posting** disclosure. It fetches only on first explicit open and remains mounted when collapsed, preserving drafts. All user, BU and CSRF-context transitions mask stale data; old GET/POST completions cannot populate the new BU context. POSTs finish rather than being cancelled; unchanged context/payload retries retain their key/body, and changed payloads receive a separate identity.

`foundation/return_models.py`, `return_services.py`, `return_views.py`, model registration and migration `0017_synthetic_sales_return_intake` add only intake, provisional-policy and append-only audit records. `src/SalesReturnIntake.tsx` and existing workbench integration provide the UI. Existing transaction services are reused only for authorization, decimal validation and idempotency, not posting. No existing financial formulas or transaction rules changed.

Captured facts:

- Originating **already delivered synthetic sale**, its customer, selected BU, brand, item/variant identity and selected returned lines/quantities.
- Return request date; declared Tivoli-showroom receipt versus warehouse collection for a large item; explicitly selected existing BU/legal-entity location and receipt/collection detail text. No location type or collection schedule/vehicle is inferred.
- Proposed QAR refund amount; original payment method explicitly recorded as **cash/card, user-recorded and not verified**, since existing simulated payments have no method field; customer's stated preference **usually original method / cash / card** and corresponding requested method.
- Every returned line's **good / not-good** inspection and notes. Intake moves only from `awaiting_inspection` to `finance_pending`. A not-good finding has no invented exclusion or disposition.

**No refund/disbursement (real or simulated), credit note, stock put-back, reservation change, valuation reversal or journal posting is performed.** No Finance-approval execution endpoint is provided: authority and treatment are not invented; Finance review/approval stays clearly pending. Existing Purchasing roles are not treated as Finance approval.

The owner-supplied **14 calendar days** is a configurable provisional per-BU rule with an explicit pending-Finance/legal source label, **not a verified statement of Qatar law**. `SalesReturnPolicy` can persist a different provisional day count; defaults are read without creating a row, and each intake keeps its rule snapshot. The date basis stays **unconfigured**; no invoice/payment/delivery baseline or eligibility calculation is assumed. There is no new policy editor or new authority to configure Finance policy.

### API, authorization and integrity

Added `GET/POST /api/purchasing/returns/`, `GET /api/purchasing/returns/sales/<quote_id>/` and `POST /api/purchasing/returns/<intake_id>/inspection/`. Reads require selected BU, and registers paginate deterministically by descending created timestamp/ID. Intake/inspection reuse the existing synthetic-user, APP_ENV=demo, active BU `create_order` and active Purchasing approval-role checks; staff alone does not grant access. Cross-BU IDs, unavailable receiving locations, revoked grants and unsupported fields/methods are denied. Location membership/legal entity are checked before register counts and inspection.

Response metadata does not include supplier cost, landed cost, stock value or movement history. Customer/item identity is derived from the originating sale, not user-supplied replacements. Quantities must be positive, distinct per source line and no greater than that sale line. This does not invent cumulative refund entitlement across multiple independent intake proposals.

Intake/inspection and audit/idempotency completion are atomic. Same key/payload returns the original result, changed payload conflicts, and current authorization is checked before replay. Inspection takes a row lock and cannot advance a reviewed intake again. A database trigger rejects return-audit updates/deletes. Tests compare **all other Foundation model rows** before/after intake and inspection, including quotes/timestamps, stock, reservations, payments, journals, reporting, grants and notification events, proving those facts stay unchanged.

## Owner-confirmed sales-return window from delivery — 2026-10-19

This section supersedes the preceding **unconfigured date basis/no window calculation** limitation only. The owner explicitly confirmed **"Confirmed; count from delivery"** and requested date-window enforcement. This is an owner-confirmed company rule, **not a verified statement of Qatar law**; legal validation remains separate.

### Implemented rule and unchanged non-posting boundaries

- Default **14 calendar days**, retaining the existing configurable per-BU `provisional_calendar_days` setting. Configuration now defaults to **`date_basis=delivery`**, and a database constraint permits only delivery. No new policy-management authority or editor was introduced.
- The only source is the sale's actual **`SalesQuote.delivered_at`**. Its calendar date is obtained using the existing Django timezone, currently **Asia/Qatar**; timezone configuration was not changed. Invoice/creation/payment dates and the Purchasing working-day calendar are not used.
- Accept only **delivery date ≤ request date ≤ delivery date + configured days**, with an inclusive deadline: default day **+14 passes**, **+15 fails**, and a request before actual delivery fails. This is calendar-date comparison, not an elapsed-hours calculation.
- The authorized source GET accepts optional `request_date=YYYY-MM-DD` and returns a server-calculated `delivery_window`. Omitted date uses the current configured-local date. POST independently reassesses and rejects an out-of-window request with **HTTP 400**, stating the actual delivery date and inclusive deadline. Failure leaves no intake, audit or idempotency row.
- An accepted intake stores delivery date, deadline, request date, captured day count, basis, date-window eligibility and validation message in `delivery_window`, alongside its existing policy snapshot. The review screen shows the stored assessment. Date-only values render as the exact server ISO dates rather than shifting with the viewer's browser timezone.
- Changing the request date starts a fresh scoped assessment, keeps the input mounted and disables submission until a matching eligible result arrives. An obsolete response cannot enable the new date. Out-of-window states show the server validation message and do not POST.
- **Date-window eligibility is not full return approval.** Existing good/not-good inspection, showroom receipt/large-item warehouse collection, proposed cash/card method and `awaiting_inspection → finance_pending` path remain. There is no new failed-inspection disposition, exception or Finance approval authority.
- No refund or disbursement, credit note, stock/reservation mutation, tax/accounting/valuation reversal, new grant or role assignment was added. Existing authorization, scoped locations, CSRF and non-posting status restrictions remain. Existing authorization/location checks precede idempotent replay.

### Existing data and replay behavior

Migration **`0018_sales_return_delivery_window`** updates existing policy configuration to delivery and derives historical intake assessments from actual delivery using each intake's captured day count. It does **not** rewrite historical policy snapshots, original idempotency results, append-only audit events, workflow status or other business/ledger data. An old historical snapshot can therefore still correctly say `unconfigured`; the new separately stored assessment and current configuration say `delivery`.

Historical records outside the confirmed window remain visible without an invented exception or disposition, but cannot newly advance inspection. Missing actual delivery produces an unavailable assessment and fails closed. Completed replay outcomes remain the original outcomes, including after a later day-count change; they are not new receipts/refunds or retroactive approvals. New keys are validated against the current rule.

## Sales-return independent-connection concurrency, retry and authorization acceptance — 2026-10-19

### Scope and result

**Closed the documented concurrent-inspection acceptance gap, without changing application logic.** Added only `foundation/test_sales_return_concurrency.py` and updated this handoff, the return specification and roadmap. No model, migration, frontend, transaction service, permission, seed or policy implementation changed.

Six new `SalesReturnConcurrencyTests` use `TransactionTestCase`, the existing synthetic Purchasing/Reporting fixtures and the real inspection endpoint. They create an isolated delivered sale and eligible non-posting intake; no existing shared users, credentials, return records or preview data are used.

1. `test_independent_inspection_keys_contend_once_and_retry_preserves_the_winner`
   - Two distinct keys propose different findings on the same intake.
   - One **HTTP 200** winner commits; the blocked contender receives the existing clear **HTTP 400**, `Inspection is already recorded; Finance review remains pending.`
   - Winner's condition/notes/quantities survive intact and match the sole inspection audit event. The rejected contender leaves no processing idempotency record.
   - An explicit identical retry returns exactly the original result; changed reuse of its key returns **HTTP 409**, `different request`. Neither changes the intake timestamp, audit facts or original outcome.
2. `test_simultaneous_identical_key_and_payload_returns_one_original_outcome`
   - Both responses are **HTTP 200** with exactly equal original results, but only one inspection transition, completed inspection key and audit event exist.
3. `test_simultaneous_conflicting_key_reuse_is_rejected_without_overwriting_outcome`
   - Same key, different inspection notes: winner **HTTP 200**, contender **HTTP 409** with a clear `different request` message, one original outcome.
4. `test_grant_revoked_after_intake_creation_denies_both_independent_inspections`
   - Revokes only the disposable fixture's existing BU `create_order` grant after intake creation.
   - Both independent requests receive the existing scope-concealing **HTTP 404**. No inspection transition, audit event or idempotency row is created.
5. `test_role_revoked_after_intake_creation_denies_both_independent_inspections`
   - Revokes only the disposable fixture's existing BU approval-role assignment after intake creation.
   - Both requests receive **HTTP 403**, with no inspection/audit/idempotency change.
6. `test_revoked_grant_prevents_completed_retry_from_disclosing_or_mutating_original_result`
   - Completes one valid inspection, revokes its fixture grant, then retries the original completed key/payload on both independent connections.
   - Both receive **HTTP 404**, without revealing line/refund data or changing the stored original outcome.

### Proof that the contention is real

Each worker owns and closes its own Django/PostgreSQL connection and calls the real `POST /api/purchasing/returns/<id>/inspection/` with a test-authenticated synthetic user. Workers verify `current_database()` equals Django's disposable `test_...` database. The observer and two workers must have **three distinct `pg_backend_pid()` values**.

For the three contention cases, a connection-local SQL execute wrapper pauses the first worker **after its real `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` acquires the lock**. The second performs its real API request; the observer explicitly queries PostgreSQL until `pg_blocking_pids(second_pid)` contains the first worker and `wait_event_type = 'Lock'`. Only then is the first released. This is not a thread-count claim, sleep-based assumption, mocked database/service result or sequential pair of API calls.

Different keys contend on the intake row. Same-key cases contend against the first transaction's uncommitted idempotency record/unique key. Permission-denied requests do not reach those locks; their `observed_lock_wait=False` is expected, not a failure of the contention tests. Every worker has bounded statement/lock/barrier waits, and test cleanup releases the held lock and closes worker connections even on failure.

Observed **full-suite** connection evidence:

| Scenario | Observer PID | Worker PIDs | PostgreSQL lock wait observed | HTTP results |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Different inspection keys | 7512 | 7514, 7516 | **True** | **200, 400** |
| Conflicting same key | 7531 | 7534, 7536 | **True** | **200, 409** |
| Identical same key | 7537 | 7540, 7542 | **True** | **200, 200** |
| Grant revoked before inspection | 7506 | 7508, 7510 | False, denied before mutation | **404, 404** |
| Role revoked before inspection | 7524 | 7528, 7529 | False, denied before mutation | **403, 403** |
| Grant revoked before completed replay | 7517 | 7520, 7522 | False, denied before replay | **404, 404** |

These PIDs are recorded test-run evidence, not persistent application identifiers.

### Non-posting and unchanged-business proof

Every accepted case asserts exactly one `finance_pending` intake, one `intake_recorded` event and one `inspection_recorded` event, with the original policy/delivery-window snapshots and intake creation time preserved. Replays/conflicts preserve the final update timestamp and audit rows. Denied new inspections leave the intake `awaiting_inspection`; denied completed replays leave it `finance_pending`.

Before/after snapshots compare **all Foundation model rows except the return-intake/policy/audit/idempotency models being deliberately exercised**. This includes the delivered quote's status and timestamps, payment facts, stock balances/movements/quantities, reservations, transfers, journals/lines, reporting records and outbox. Revocation-test snapshots are taken after their intentional fixture-only revocation, proving the inspection/replay attempts add no further business or access mutations.

No new grant or role is assigned beyond the unchanged existing test-fixture setup. No refund/disbursement (even simulated), credit note, stock disposition/put-back, accounting/valuation reversal, Finance approval authority or exception is introduced.

**Completed the return-form native-browser usability gap above.** Concurrent intake-creation replay remains a separate gap; no Finance, stock, return-window or access policy was changed.

### Tests and isolated environment

Added `scripts/sales-return-browser.test.mjs` using the existing dependency-free Chromium/CDP and `node:test` harness. Added the explicit `npm run test:sales-return-browser` entry point (build plus five tests). No dependency, browser or other tool was installed/downloaded.

The harness serves the real production-built React app from `dist/` on an OS-assigned **127.0.0.1** port. Test-only `/api/auth/me/` and CSRF responses provide a fictional identity and placeholder token; there is no application auth bypass, real login, credential or role assignment. The test fixture permits only authorized-BU synthetic return GETs and two exact in-memory mock POST paths: `/api/purchasing/returns/` and `/api/purchasing/returns/19/inspection/`. Those mock POSTs capture requests and return validation/Finance-pending responses, never proxy to Django or a database. Unknown paths, non-allowlisted writes, unexpected scope and external page requests fail the tests. Owned browser profiles/processes and loopback servers close after each test, including assertion failures.

Exact new test names:

1. **`return intake native tab order, accessible names and client/server validation announcements`**
   - Keyboard-opens the existing native return disclosure; fills the delivered-sale ID using Chromium input.
   - Native Tab order covers returned quantity, native date segments, receiving mode/location, proposed amount, original method, preference, read-only requested method, collection notes and submit. Checks real `:focus-visible`, computed outlines of at least 2px and at least **3:1** contrast.
   - Verifies wrapped labels plus key accessible names in Chromium's actual accessibility tree.
   - Invalid quantity produces a `role=alert` client validation message with **zero mock POSTs**. Correcting it and submitting produces the distinct mock-server validation alert, with exactly one in-memory POST.
2. **`inspection native keyboard, error announcement, safe retry and Finance-pending status feedback`**
   - Checks accessible names for condition, notes and Close; uses native Space/Arrow/Enter, Tab and Enter submission rather than React event simulation.
   - A mocked 400 must announce **Inspection not recorded**, retain notes and expose an accessibility-tree alert.
   - An explicit retry sends exactly the original key, payload and endpoint; exactly two mock requests occur. Mock success announces **Synthetic inspection recorded**, exposes a `status` role, shows pending Finance review and removes the inspection submit action. No refund, credit, stock or disposition behavior exists in the fixture or was enabled.
3. **`return forms 1280px: no page overflow, labeled reachable controls and locally scrollable register`**
4. **`return forms 390px: no page overflow, labeled reachable controls and locally scrollable register`**
5. **`return forms 320px: no page overflow, labeled reachable controls and locally scrollable register`**
   - Geometry runs at height 844px; desktop keyboard tests use the harness default 1280×900.
   - Compare document `scrollWidth <= clientWidth` strictly, including native scrollbar space. Verify at least 100px inspection-heading width, labeled controls, in-viewport geometry and actual hit-testing after scrolling each control into view.
   - The wide register has its own `overflow-x:auto`, not page overflow.
   - Check native inspection Tab/Shift+Tab focus and keyboard Close at every width, without any mock POST.

### Reproduced defects and minimal corrections

- **Incorrect operation announcement:** the inspection regression failed on the existing `Intake not recorded` heading. Both error and success headings used intake wording regardless of action. `SalesReturnIntake.tsx` now tags only its in-memory outcome presentation with `intake`/`inspection`; inspection feedback has the correct heading. Endpoints, payloads, keys, request/context guards and transactions are unchanged.
- **Mobile inspection header:** screenshot inspection and a strengthened geometry assertion showed the heading squeezed to **8.09375px** beside Close at 320px. Mobile-only CSS gives the heading and Close separate grid rows and reduces excess nested padding. The verified heading is **104px** wide at 320px.
- **Native-scrollbar/page overflow:** the original 320px body minimum forced `scrollWidth=320` against `clientWidth=305`. A read-side synthetic badge and the outer prototype badge also exceeded available space. CSS now allows the body to fit its available width **only at mobile widths while the return component exists**, allows the prototype badge to wrap in that same context, and wraps the existing read-side header within this return workbench context. It does not hide overflowing page content or alter the normal sidebar/other-page baseline.

An initial browser harness assumption about native select popups and focus after disabling a submit button was corrected in the test interactions; it was not treated as an application defect. Final tests use actual selection/focus assertions and explicit focus setup before the deliberate retry.

## Concurrent return-intake creation and retry acceptance — 2026-10-19

Closed the previously documented concurrent **creation** gap, separately from the
earlier inspection-concurrency and browser-usability increments. Added only two
tests to `foundation/test_sales_return_concurrency.py` and documentation. No
application, frontend, model, migration, permission or policy code changed; both
new tests passed on their first run, so no implementation correction was needed.

### Exact new tests and assertions

- `SalesReturnCreationConcurrencyTests.test_simultaneous_identical_intakes_commit_one_audit_and_replay_original`
  sends simultaneous identical requests to the actual `/api/purchasing/returns/`
  API with the same key. Both return **200**, with identical complete results;
  exactly one intake, one `intake_recorded` event and one completed
  `sales_return_intake` idempotency record exist. Two further explicit retries
  return that original result without changing the intake, timestamps, event or
  idempotency facts.
- `SalesReturnCreationConcurrencyTests.test_simultaneous_conflicting_intake_payload_rejects_loser_without_partial_writes`
  uses the same key with distinct proposed synthetic refund amounts. The first
  request returns **200**, the competing request **409**, with the existing
  “different request” message. Subsequent conflicting reuse is also **409** and
  the original retry returns **200** with the original complete result.
  The rejected request leaves no partial intake/event/processing record and
  cannot overwrite the winner.

Both reuse the existing real-lock scheduling harness: separate worker connections
and observer connection, synchronized workers, first worker held after a real
idempotency-row `SELECT FOR UPDATE`, and `pg_blocking_pids` plus
`wait_event_type=Lock` proving actual second-worker contention. No SQL result,
service or endpoint is mocked. Initial focused-run PIDs:

| Case | Observer | Workers | Observed lock wait | Responses |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Conflicting payload | 19627 | 19720, 19722 | true | 200, 409 |
| Identical payload | 19730 | 19733, 19734 | true | 200, 200 |

Before/after snapshots compare every Foundation model except the intentionally
exercised return intake/event/idempotency/policy models, as in the existing
inspection acceptance harness. Thus delivery status/timestamps, payment facts,
stock balances/movements, reservations, journals and all other business/access
records are unchanged. Intake/event/idempotency rows are separately checked for
exact counts, contents and no changes on subsequent retry/conflict. The accepted
intake remains **awaiting inspection**, not Finance-approved; no inspection is
performed by these new tests and nothing is posted.

## Local synthetic operations-monitoring foundation — 2026-10-19

Implemented `python manage.py monitor_synthetic_integrity`, an operator-only
command combining the unchanged stock-quantity, transfer-pair and posted-journal
diagnostics in that fixed order. See `SYNTHETIC_OPERATIONS_MONITORING.md`.
Implementation is in `foundation/operations_monitoring.py` and
`foundation/management/commands/monitor_synthetic_integrity.py`; there is no
HTTP/UI endpoint, schema change, scheduler, network sink or persisted run history.

### Behavior and snapshot contract

The deterministic JSON explicitly labels **SYNTHETIC DATA ONLY**. Each check has
`execution: passed` or `failed_to_run`; successfully executed checks separately
report `empty`, `no_discrepancies` or `discrepancies`. Failed checks have null
results, `outcome: unavailable` and only a sanitized exception type/fixed message,
not raw SQL or arbitrary exception text. Later independent checks still run.
The discrepancy count is explicitly limited to **completed** checks.

Top-level failure takes precedence over detected discrepancies. All successful
empty/consistent checks exit 0; discrepancies or execution failure emit JSON then
raise `CommandError` (CLI exit 1). Unsafe global preflight targets/outer
transactions are rejected before any check runs.

**There is no shared snapshot across the three checks.** Each unchanged
diagnostic uses its own PostgreSQL `REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY` transaction.
The output sets `shared_snapshot: false` and describes that scope. An intervening
commit can appear in later checks; the summary never compares cross-check
generations or claims a point-in-time cross-ledger reconciliation.

### Seven new PostgreSQL tests

All are in `foundation.test_operations_monitoring.SyntheticOperationsMonitoringTests`:

1. `test_empty_checks_are_successfully_executed_not_failed_or_nonempty`
2. `test_healthy_summary_is_deterministic_and_reads_without_writes`
3. `test_detected_discrepancies_are_not_execution_failures_or_repaired`
4. `test_database_execution_failure_is_unavailable_redacted_and_other_checks_continue`
5. `test_all_three_transactions_enforce_repeatable_read_and_reject_writes`
6. `test_safety_preflight_refuses_unsafe_targets_and_existing_transactions`
7. `test_separate_snapshots_are_explicit_when_writer_commits_between_checks`

Healthy receipt/reservation/transfer fixtures exercise all three real diagnostic
implementations. Two runs have byte-identical JSON, only SELECT/transaction-control
SQL, and identical before/after rows for **every Foundation model**.
The discrepancy case uses an allowed test-only inconsistent balance; no database
protection is disabled. The failure case forces actual PostgreSQL division by
zero at the transfer read, proving rollback, unavailable/redacted output,
non-successful command outcome and successful subsequent journal verification.

Another test checks actual isolation/read-only settings and attempts a forbidden
UPDATE inside a rollback-only test savepoint in **each of the three
transactions**; PostgreSQL rejects all three. Row snapshots remain identical.
The separate-snapshot test commits a real synthetic receipt through another
connection/backend PID between completed stock and later journal checks: stock
correctly reports its earlier empty snapshot, journals see the receipt, and the
next run sees both. That fixture writer is explicitly test-only, not part of the
command.

## Read-only synthetic notification-outbox health summary — 2026-10-19

Implemented the separate local operator command:

```sh
python manage.py summarize_notification_outbox_health
```

Implementation is in `foundation/outbox_health.py` and the matching management
command. See `SYNTHETIC_NOTIFICATION_OUTBOX_HEALTH.md`. No existing worker,
enqueue, three-check integrity-monitor, API, permission, business-service or
frontend implementation changed. No model/migration was added.

### Exact behavior

- Separate counts for `pending`, `retry`, `dry_run_recorded`, `dry_run_failed`,
  including explicit zero keys.
- Total intents, sum of stored attempt counters, distribution of intents by
  existing attempt counts 0–3, and the existing worker limit of three.
- Aggregate failure-code counts: `FAKE_SINK_FAILURE` is the only literal
  allowlisted worker code. Unknown nonempty strings become
  `REDACTED_UNRECOGNIZED` inside SQL; raw strings are not fetched or printed.
- No event `message`/`details`, recipients, channels, customer/quote values,
  names, identifiers or payloads are selected or emitted.
- Explicit synthetic/dry-run-only labeling and
  `external_notification_sent_by_this_command: false`,
  `external_delivery_verified: false`. Recorded fake-sink intent is not external
  delivery; no delivered-count metric is fabricated.
- Deterministic sorted-key JSON; no changing timestamps, age/overdue thresholds,
  severity policy or schedules.

Both scope validation and grouped metadata reads use **one database-enforced
REPEATABLE READ, READ ONLY snapshot**. The command rejects an outer transaction,
unsafe environment/database/host and out-of-scope related synthetic facts or
unsupported notification-event kinds. It never filters away a scope violation
and reports the remaining rows as a successful complete count.

Exit 0 means successful metadata retrieval, not approval of pending/failed work
or evidence of external delivery. State is `empty` or `recorded_metadata`;
nonzero failed-intent counts do not trigger invented health/severity thresholds.
Safety/scope errors fail without a partial JSON report.

### Seven new disposable PostgreSQL tests

All are in `foundation.test_outbox_health.NotificationOutboxHealthTests`:

1. `test_empty_explicit_zero_counts_and_no_external_delivery_claim`
2. `test_mixed_counts_attempts_safe_codes_and_deterministic_redacted_output`
3. `test_no_worker_network_payload_read_or_database_writes`
4. `test_read_only_repeatable_read_is_enforced_by_postgresql`
5. `test_scope_rejection_and_database_protection_of_synthetic_related_facts`
6. `test_unsafe_environment_target_or_existing_transaction_is_rejected`
7. `test_concurrent_commit_cannot_mix_scope_check_and_group_counts`

The mixed fixture includes both existing readiness/storage event kinds and six
intents: **2 pending / 2 retry / 1 dry_run_recorded / 1 dry_run_failed**.
Stored attempt total is **8**, distribution **0:2 / 1:1 / 2:2 / 3:1**.
Known-code count is **2**, redacted unknown-code count **1**; messages,
recipient/cost sentinels and arbitrary error strings never appear in JSON.
Repeated runs are byte-identical.

No-write proof compares every Foundation model row before/after the command and
allows only SELECT/transaction-control SQL. Worker invocation, fake-sink recording
and socket connections are guarded against. SQL capture proves neither message
nor details columns are selected. Another test verifies transaction settings and
PostgreSQL rejection of a deliberately attempted update inside a rollback-only
test savepoint. No database protection is disabled.

Synthetic-scope coverage includes actual refusal of the unsupported
`storage_exception` kind, unsafe environment/target refusal, and PostgreSQL's
existing constraint rejection of attempts to mark intent, event, quote, BU,
legal entity or customer non-synthetic. Invalid non-synthetic rows are not forced
past database constraints just to build fixtures.

The snapshot regression uses a genuinely independent writer/backend PID. After
the reader's scope check, it atomically changes pending → retry and adds a
failed intent. The current summary still sees **1 pending / 0 attempts**, while
the next run sees **1 retry + 1 failed / 4 attempts**. These are explicit
test-fixture writes, not health-command worker execution or side effects.

## Local read-only synthetic backup-evidence summary — 2026-10-19

Implemented `scripts/backup_evidence.py`, documented in
`SYNTHETIC_BACKUP_EVIDENCE.md` and linked from the portability guide/roadmap:

```sh
python -B scripts/backup_evidence.py \
  --bundle /explicit/local/synthetic/bundle --synthetic \
  --observed-at 2026-10-19T12:00:00+00:00
```

This is a standalone standard-library script, **not a Django management command**.
It never loads environment/credential files, connects to PostgreSQL, runs a
backup/restore runner, starts services, extracts media to disk, schedules work or
sends notifications. `--bundle` is explicit and required; `--synthetic` attests
synthetic-only operator input. No real backup or company file was inspected.

### Implemented evidence and safeguards

- Required/optional artifact presence, sizes and readable schema-v1 manifest
  metadata. Database metadata is aggregate table/row/migration counts and declared
  PostgreSQL major, not table/migration/database names, credentials or dump data.
- Reuses `scripts/backup_artifacts.py` checksum verification through an explicit
  safe digest callback. Added optional arguments without changing the default
  checksum caller behavior.
- The existing media verifier's default path extracts temporary files and is
  therefore **not used by this command**. Added an explicit `inspect_only`
  streaming path, with shared archive checks: no filesystem extraction; validates
  safe regular-file members, normalized paths, duplicate/path conflicts,
  permission bits, declared counts/sizes, readable member lengths and gzip CRC/
  trailer integrity. Default restore/extraction behavior is unchanged.
- Filesystem mtime and ctime are labeled observations only (ctime is metadata
  change, not creation). An explicit timezone-aware observation time makes JSON
  deterministic; no acceptable-age threshold or inferred backup-completion time.
- Strict filename/manifest/checksum allowlists, duplicate-key/schema validation
  and a 1MiB technical JSON bound; missing/malformed/incomplete/tampered evidence
  has fixed redacted issue codes, never raw exceptions, paths or payloads.
- Directory-descriptor-relative `O_NOFOLLOW` reads, refusal of symlink ancestors,
  symlink/hardlinked artifacts, special files and parent traversal; identity/
  metadata/membership comparisons reject observed concurrent changes.
- Linux `O_NOATIME` prevents evidence-read access-time mutation. Unsupported
  platforms or insufficient permission fail closed, without ordinary-read
  fallback. Bytecode caching is disabled by the script; `-B` is also documented.

Success is `artifact_integrity_verified`, exit 0. Missing/invalid/unsafe evidence
returns exit 1. Every result states **artifact integrity does not establish
restore recoverability** and keeps `restore_recoverability: not_established`.
The fake/nonempty dump is opaque bytes; no `pg_restore --list`, SQL/schema
validation, real restore, signature/origin authentication or cross-artifact
transaction-consistency proof is claimed.

### Sixteen temporary synthetic file-fixture tests

All are in `scripts.test_backup_evidence.BackupEvidenceTests`:

1. `test_complete_no_media_bundle_and_deterministic_observation_metadata`
2. `test_media_inspection_reuses_verifiers_without_extracting_or_running_restore`
3. `test_missing_required_artifacts_and_missing_optional_declared_media`
4. `test_malformed_duplicate_or_unsupported_manifests_never_look_verified`
5. `test_tampered_dump_or_media_is_not_integrity_or_recoverability_success`
6. `test_incomplete_checksums_and_unexpected_manifest_entries_are_rejected`
7. `test_reject_non_synthetic_manifest_attestation_and_invalid_observation_time`
8. `test_symlink_ancestors_artifacts_hardlinks_special_files_and_parent_paths_rejected`
9. `test_unsafe_archive_members_and_metadata_mismatch_are_rejected_without_extraction`
10. `test_corrupt_gzip_trailer_is_not_verified_even_with_updated_checksums`
11. `test_empty_dump_inconsistent_media_and_extra_files_are_incomplete`
12. `test_redaction_in_success_errors_and_cli_output`
13. `test_no_mutations_database_subprocess_network_or_extraction_including_atime`
14. `test_permission_or_noatime_failure_is_redacted_and_never_falls_back`
15. `test_concurrent_artifact_replacement_is_rejected`
16. `test_legacy_checksum_and_no_media_verifier_entrypoints_remain_compatible`

Fixtures use only temporary synthetic files, including an intentionally opaque
fake dump, small in-memory-generated archives and sentinel strings. No pg_dump/
backup script is invoked. Malformed archives include traversal/absolute paths,
links, duplicates/conflicts, unsafe modes and a corrupt gzip trailer whose
updated SHA256 still matches—proving media validity is not inferred from hashes.

The mutation test blocks write-mode opens, file/directory mutations, subprocess
entrypoints, socket connections, database/ORM imports, temporary extraction
directories and archive extraction methods while the summary runs. Before/after
evidence metadata includes **nanosecond atime, mtime and ctime**. Existing
default checksum/no-media verification entrypoints also pass compatibility
tests; the default no-media path creates a test-only temporary directory but
extracts no media file. It is never called by the new summary.

| `npm test` | **193 passed, 0 failures/skips**, all 12 frontend runner groups. |

| `npm run test:contrast` | **105 PASS**, no failures. |

### Deliberately not run and remaining limits

- **No PostgreSQL/backend suite, real backup/restore proof or Django database/
  migration commands were run**, honoring the explicit prohibition on database
  connections, services and restores in this slice. The preceding **253
  PostgreSQL passes** are historical, not fresh evidence for this change.
  Models/migrations/application APIs were not changed.
- No UI changed; no browser verification, authentication, shared preview access
  or workflow restart occurred. Frontend checks are regression evidence only.
- Actual restore/media-extraction interoperability was not rerun. The old
  defaults are retained and isolated checksum/no-media entrypoints pass, but
  this is not a newly executed end-to-end restore.
- Linux no-atime permissions are required. Permission denial is tested through
  injected OS failure, not changing another user's permissions or credentials.
  Metadata/race checks do not provide an atomic filesystem snapshot or defeat a
  privileged attacker. The operator must supply genuinely local storage; a
  local-looking pathname cannot by itself prove mount locality.
- Synthetic attestation/name checks cannot prove opaque dump contents.
  Unkeyed checksums do not authenticate source. Resource isolation for hostile
  giant archives, backup-age targets, retention, storage/encryption/key choices,
  RPO/RTO, schedules and production recovery approval are not added or inferred.
- No production data, credentials, network services, privacy/sharing settings,
  publishing, user assignments or company policy were accessed/changed.

## Delivery & After-Sales operations and quantity progress — 2026-10-19

### Inspected acceptance gaps and implemented independent scope

Inspected `MILESTONE_ROADMAP.md`, Milestone 3 and architecture specs, purchasing/
delivery/return services, quote read/write handlers, current workbench and tests.
Two concrete gaps were independent of missing Finance/company policy:

1. The existing **Delivery & After-Sales** destination still rendered
   `PLANNED · NOT IMPLEMENTED`, despite existing authenticated operations.
2. Quote detail omitted stored delivery progress and actual readiness/handover
   timestamps, leaving an operator without a direct per-line reconciliation
   view even though the models already maintained these facts.

Completed both without adding another monitoring utility:

- `App` now renders the existing Purchasing Workbench in focused delivery mode.
  Reuses existing quote/context/selection ownership and idempotent action logic.
  Procurement/commitment/receipt/quote-creation forms and unrelated directory/
  procurement reads are excluded. Default Purchasing mode remains unchanged.
- Existing simulated quote collections, readiness, whole-quote delivery,
  approved deferred-balance terms, storage operations, quote/storage/reservation/
  delivery registers and synthetic return intake are available through this
  business section subject to their unchanged server/state/configuration gates.
  A denied report register does not inherit permission from quote access.
- Existing staff-only configuration remains necessary for authorized deferred-
  balance/storage exception role gates; ordinary users never fetch it. Hiding
  configuration display does not suppress a dependency needed by an already
  permitted operation or assume a missing role.
- Existing Delivery sidebar identity/favorite destination is unchanged; child
  links target real areas, including the specific native return disclosure
  rather than a generic workbench panel.
- `GET /api/purchasing/quotes/<id>/?business_unit_id=<id>` adds a read-only
  `delivery_progress` object under the existing quote authorization:
  `ready_at`, `delivered_at`, and ordered PK line records with `quote_line_id`,
  `variant_id`, `ordered_quantity`, `reserved_to_date_quantity`,
  `delivered_quantity`, `remaining_quantity`.
- Decimal strings come directly from stored Decimal quantities; remaining is
  ordered minus delivered. UI does no floating-point recalculation. Historical
  quote-line reservation coverage is explicitly **not active reserved stock**.
  No cost/value/supplier/history field is introduced.
- Existing delivery/payment services, write request/response contracts, retry
  identities, approvals, accounting/valuation, permissions and seeded data are
  unchanged. After an approved balance collection, the delivered state and
  original handover timestamp remain intact; no second delivery is offered.

See `DELIVERY_AFTER_SALES_WORKBENCH.md` for the requirement mapping. The business
entry point is implemented; **this does not claim complete policy-dependent
Delivery & After-Sales or production acceptance**.

## Bounded cross-section sensitive-data review

### Confirmed disclosure and correction

The receipt POST acknowledgement and its idempotent replay returned private
supplier/landed values to a `create_order` actor without cost data grants.
The new regression uses a commitment with a stored synthetic QAR 987.65 unit
price and deliberately omits that price from the receipt request: the leak
was not merely an echo of caller-entered values. The pre-fix
`test_receipt_ack_and_retry_do_not_disclose_stored_commitment_cost_without_grants`
failed on `purchase_value`, `eligible_landed_charges`,
`landed_cost_rate_percent`, `landed_cost_allocations`, and `inventory_value`.
Exploratory fixture/contract assertion errors are not classified as disclosures.

`PurchaseReceiptCreateView` now projects its HTTP response using the existing
receipt-register cost scopes, including active role grants and the receipt BU:

- No cost authority, or staff status alone: receipt/journal/movement IDs,
  optional commitment ID, and currency only.
- `supplier_cost`: purchase value; `landed_cost`: eligible charges/allocations.
- Both scopes: composite inventory value and landed-cost rate.
- Recheck on every response/replay; wrong-BU or revoked grants do not authorize
  values. The private idempotency result, calculations and posting records are
  unchanged. The previous delivery-acknowledgement cost projection remains intact.

No permission or workflow rule was added. Three older lifecycle/procurement
tests expected private costs in unprivileged responses; those assertions now
require masking and verify the same calculations through the isolated private
idempotency record, rather than granting their actors cost access.

## Retail collection follow-up worklist — synthetic and read-only

### Implemented scope and preserved boundaries

- New `GET /api/purchasing/collections/` and focused
  `#/retail/collections` / **Retail → Collection follow-up**. Function Favorite
  `retail.collections` uses the existing per-user Favorites API; section
  Favorites remain valid.
- Reuses `_purchasing_unit_for_user`: active synthetic BU, synthetic demo actor,
  active `create_order` and existing per-BU approval-role requirements. Staff,
  stock access, panel assignment or a Favorite alone never grant collection
  access. No purchasing/payment service or permission mapping changed.
- Correlated PostgreSQL `SUM` of recorded **DEPOSIT/BALANCE** payments only,
  with decimal money expressions and two-decimal strings. Storage payments,
  private idempotency results, costs, journals and illustrative report facts
  are not collection sources. No payment-by-line joins or N+1 payment lookups.
- Default positive-remaining filter, optional fully collected rows, exact
  positive quote-ID search, refresh and server pagination. Filters precede
  count/slice; order is `-created_at, -pk`. Optional API `location_id` validates
  explicit synthetic BU/legal-entity location membership and matches quote
  lines with `EXISTS`; displayed amounts remain **whole-quote**, not allocated
  location revenue. It adds no capacity/report/location-to-user authority.
- Explicit response allowlist: `quote_id`, `kind`, `status`, `currency`,
  `total_quote_value`, `recorded_collections`, `remaining_balance`, `ready_at`,
  `delivered_at`. No customer directory, supplier/cost/history payload or
  payment-account information is exposed.
- Row navigation selects the quote through existing lookup and opens existing
  collection actions. It creates no payment and does not remount transaction
  forms, alter draft/retry identity, permit an otherwise denied payment, or
  rewrite delivered state.
- UI labels amounts as simulated recorded prototype collections, **not real
  payments, receivables, overdue amounts or new credit terms**. Quote status is
  shown: a positive value on a pending/cancelled quote is not authority to
  collect. Existing actions retain their own gates.
- Empty/error/401/403/concealed-404 states clear rows; first committed BU/user
  context changes mask previous data, and obsolete successes/failures cannot
  replace current state. No collection GET while its focused view is inactive.
  Current permissions are checked on each load/reload/action, not by a new
  live revocation push service.
- New surfaces, accents, hover and focus use existing per-BU/custom palette
  tokens. No new due dates, refund/credit rules, terms, grants, user assignments,
  report policy, hold blocking or procurement access interpretation were added.

## Finance reconciliation and isolated draft foundation — 2026-10-20

**Completed bounded deliverable, not completion of Finance.** This closes the
resumed scaffolding task with a requirement matrix, isolated schema/services,
functional bilingual prototype and current verification. It does not activate
Finance for shared users.

### What was documented versus implemented

- The supplied broad GL/AP/AR/cash-bank/assets/budgets/tax/expenses/close/
  project/approvals/integration requirements were **roadmap coverage**, not a
  functioning Finance workspace. Existing `LedgerAccount`/posted journals are
  synthetic stock-transaction foundations; `JournalEntry.DRAFT` is transient
  and cannot remain unposted at commit under existing DB protections. Reporting
  budgets/expense panels, quote collections and controlled exports are not AP,
  AR, expense processing or Finance account administration.
- [FINANCE_REQUIREMENTS_RECONCILIATION.md](FINANCE_REQUIREMENTS_RECONCILIATION.md)
  now maps every supplied scope group to actual code/tests, missing work,
  dependencies and a bounded next deliverable. It retains cash forecasting,
  facilities/loans, BU shared-cost reporting, factory costing, payroll
  integration, controlled exports and migration planning. The company boundary
  is one legal entity with BU dimensions; no multi-company operation is inferred.

  scope source is the owner's supplied list plus the existing specs/roadmap;
  no claim is made that a missing attachment was independently reviewed.

### New implemented scope and safeguards

- `FinanceDraftAccount`, `FinanceDraftDimension`, dimension values, draft
  journals/lines and line-dimension links are separate from operational
  `LedgerAccount`/`JournalEntry`/`JournalLine`. Account/dimension/value codes have
  explicit `TEST-DRAFT-` prefixes; all six new tables are synthetic-only.
- `foundation/finance_drafts.py` creates account/dimension proposals and
  persists draft journals atomically in isolated tests. Amounts are exact,
  finite, non-negative, bounded two-decimal values; floating-point input is
  rejected. Drafts may remain incomplete/unbalanced for review. The read-only
  review reports line issues and exact debit/credit totals. No posting or
  approval function exists and the DB rejects changing a draft to `posted`.
- Each journal has one synthetic legal entity. Existing BU dimensions and
  proposed dimension values must belong to that entity; no cross-entity
  association or implicit allocation is accepted.
- **No Finance authorization exists in the current action model.** Staff,
  superuser, report-manager, capacity and purchasing powers are not re-used.
  There is no Finance API, Django-admin registration, app import, sidebar or
  Favorite activation. `default_permissions = ()` prevents new implicit Django
  model permissions. No assignments/grants were added.
- Persistence fails closed unless `APP_ENV=demo`, the explicit test-only
  `FINANCE_DRAFT_TEST_MODE=True` setting and a PostgreSQL `test_*` database are
  all present. The normal shared app does not enable that test setting.
- `src/FinanceDraftWorkspace.tsx` and `prototypes/finance-drafts/` provide the
  **standalone local-session** English/Arabic editor: proposed accounts,
  dimensions/values, optional synthetic BU dimensions, add/edit/remove lines,
  memos, exact totals, actionable validation, per-line review and local-session
  snapshots. Arabic values are explicit input, not invented translations.
  Input changes invalidate the prior review without erasing drafts.
- The local editor makes **no network requests** and is **not wired to backend
  persistence**. Its local snapshots disappear on reload. This separation is
  intentional until Finance access/API authority is approved; it is not an
  authenticated shared Finance workflow.

## Connected isolated Finance draft workflow — 2026-10-20

**Completed bounded batch.** The bilingual editor now uses real persistence in
a dedicated disposable environment. This is not shared Finance activation,
whole-Finance completion, team acceptance or production readiness.

### Delivered workflow

- `FinanceDraftLab.tsx` connects the existing bilingual editor through
  `finance-draft-lab-api.ts` to real Django/PostgreSQL: proposed account and
  dimension/value setup, journal save, saved-draft list, page reload/reopen,
  editing, exact review and revision history. No session-only save is described
  as persistent. Multiple dimension values per line survive reopening/editing.
- Drafts remain draft-only. Current fixed QAR values are the existing synthetic
  test invariant, not production currency/accounting configuration. Existing
  operational accounts, journals, stock, collections and reservations are not
  touched.
- A new journal records revision 1 and its full snapshot. Edits use
  `select_for_update()` plus an exact `expected_revision`; only one simultaneous
  same-base edit can commit. The loser receives HTTP **409**, with its editor
  inputs retained and an explicit confirm-before-discard reload action.
- Migration `0024_finance_draft_revisions` adds draft revision metadata and a
  separate snapshot table, with unique journal/revision, synthetic-only
  constraints, no default Django model permissions and a PostgreSQL trigger
  rejecting revision UPDATE/DELETE. Snapshots retain original titles, line
  references/names, BU/dimension codes, amounts, memos and review results.
  Legacy isolated drafts get an actual revision-0 baseline on first edit;
  earlier history is not invented. Migration-initialized metadata is not proof
  of a historical business date.
- Replacement lines, title/version updates and revision insertion are atomic.
  A forced revision-insert failure preserves the entire previous draft and
  history. Saved history is not an approval, posted journal or an accounting
  audit certification.
- Validation and stale-edit errors retain local inputs. A transient refresh
  failure preserves authorized content; confirmed synthetic-session denial
  removes setup, editor and history. Pending saves disable competing controls,
  preserve editor identity and warn on unload; add/remove-line edits also trigger
  the unsaved-work warning.
- A lost save response is labeled **unknown outcome**: it might have committed.
  The editor blocks another save until explicit list/reopen recovery. There
  are no automatic retries. A committed save followed by a list-refresh failure
  is still reported as saved, not as a failed transaction.

### Precise isolation and access boundary

- The normal `config.urls` does **not** include the new
  `foundation.finance_lab_urls`. The shared App/sidebar/Favorites/admin remain
  unchanged and Finance remains unfinished there.
- `config.finance_lab_settings` can be used only with a dedicated
  `/tmp/tivoli-finance-lab.*/data` target and PostgreSQL `test_*` database. The
  runner pins **PG16.15**, database `test_finance_lab`, PG port **55167** and
  Django HTTP **127.0.0.1:18069**. Before setup it verifies actual
  `data_directory`; it also proves the HTTP listener belongs to its child
  Django process. Each request independently checks the configured actual data
  directory, explicit lab/test flags, synthetic entity and test DB.
- The runner unsets shared DSN/secret inputs and explicitly supplies its own
  local connection. It creates only one fictional nonstaff/non-superuser actor
  with an **unusable password**, one synthetic entity and two BU dimension
  choices; **zero memberships or grants**. It runs no `seed_demo`.
- “Open isolated synthetic test session” creates a real Django session for that
  single fixed test actor, with normal CSRF enforcement on writes. No password
  is created, revealed or reset. Other actors, ordinary staff/superuser
  authority, inactive actors and a disabled/unverified lab do not get access.
  This is explicit **test access**, not ordinary ERP password authentication or
  an approved production Finance permission scheme.
- The isolated API filters to the fixture's one entity and validates every
  account/BU/dimension reference. It does not define multi-user draft ownership
  or actual Finance scope/assignment rules.
- PostgreSQL saves survive browser reload and reopening in another browser
  session while the runner exists. **The entire database is deliberately
  deleted when the runner exits**; no persistence across runner restarts,
  production durability or restore recovery is claimed.
- Migrations **0023 and 0024** were applied only in disposable databases by this
  work. No shared schema query, migration, seed/reset, actual account/grant/
  credential change or shared transaction was performed. No managed workflow
  start/restart was issued. No lasting `.replit` change was made.

## Isolated recurring-journal template proposals — 2026-10-20

**Completed bounded isolated prototype batch; not Finance section completion,
shared-user activation, team acceptance or production readiness.**

### Actual functionality and boundaries

- The existing bilingual persisted lab now has **New recurring template** and
  separate **Open template** choices. It reuses draft accounts, dimensions,
  exact line amounts, optional same-entity BU choices and the existing synthetic
  session. No new shared route, authority, permission or actual assignment.
- Each template requires an explicit inclusive range and explicit YYYY-MM-DD
  occurrence dates. The common entered lines/amounts repeat unchanged on exactly
  those dates. There is no frequency selector/generator, implicit first date,
  month-end/leap-day adjustment, timezone conversion, workday rule, recognition,
  FX, approval or scheduler. Dates are proposals, not effective posting periods.
- Reject invalid/reversed ranges, missing/ambiguous/invalid dates, duplicates,
  unordered/out-of-range dates and unsupported convention keys. Preserve exact
  decimal, entity/account/BU/dimension validation. 100 dates / 200 lines are
  **technical limits**, not accounting/company policy.
- Real save/list/reload/reopen/edit; versioned date metadata and line snapshots;
  stale edits return HTTP 409 without lost updates. A saved draft's kind cannot
  switch. Date/amount/history insertion is atomic; a forced history failure
  rolls it all back. Existing immutable-history protections remain.
- **Preview saved proposed occurrences** reads only the saved balanced revision:
  dates, each balanced occurrence's totals, aggregate exact proposed totals,
  and common entry lines with account/BU/dimensions/memos. Unsaved edits must be
  saved first, and changing inputs clears old preview. Preview makes no
  occurrence, job, journal, audit or other business records.
- The preview API holds the existing parent-row lock for coherent lines/version;
  tests prove no SQL INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE. This is application read-only
  behavior, not a claim that PostgreSQL runs the whole request in READ ONLY
  transaction mode.
- Existing pending/unsaved safeguards, transient-error input preservation,
  actual session-denial clearing and unknown-save recovery remain. Lost save
  responses block another save until explicit list/reopen recovery; no automatic
  retries or exactly-once create guarantee is claimed.
- Migration **0025_finance_recurring_proposals** adds draft kind/proposal JSON
  and its constraint. Defaults preserve ordinary journal drafts; immutable
  previous snapshots are not backfilled or rewritten. Applied **only to
  disposable databases**. No shared schema state was queried or changed.

## Explicit-input accrual/prepayment adjustment proposals — 2026-10-20

### Actual implemented workflow

The isolated English Finance lab now has **New accrual proposal** and
**New prepayment proposal** actions and a separately identified saved adjustment
register. Each requires a user-entered proposed calendar date, nonblank explicit
explanation (2,000-character technical limit), title and existing synthetic draft
account/dimension/optional same-entity BU lines. Quantities here are exact debit/
credit money strings, not inferred recognition calculations.

The reviewer enters every proposed amount and account. There is no period
selection/default, amortization duration, allocation convention, residual
distribution, offset mapping, exchange/tax rule or approval authority. The UI
clearly identifies proposals, not scheduled or posted entries. Missing/ambiguous
dates and explanations, excessive amount precision, foreign choices and extra
convention keys in proposal metadata are rejected. A proposal's kind cannot be
silently changed after it is saved.

Entered lines are reviewed with exact totals and signed debit-minus-credit
difference, using the existing Python Decimal/BigInt handling. The existing UI
requires valid balanced review before save; the API can retain unbalanced drafts
for **review only**, without adding a balancing line. No imports, automatic
journals, scheduling or ledger posting were enabled.

Saving persists date/explanation/lines in disposable PostgreSQL; browser reload
and explicit reopen restore them. Editing records a new immutable snapshot.
Row locking and expected revisions reject stale edits (HTTP 409) without lost
updates; validation/conflict feedback retains local metadata and amounts.
Explicit reload replaces local edits only after the existing confirmation.
Unknown-save handling still blocks automatic retry and replacement submission.
Ordinary journal, opening worksheet and recurring proposal functionality remains.

Internal controls remain English; optional supplied Arabic business text is
retained. Customer quotation/invoice renderers, historical issued snapshots and
all operational stock/payment/journal behavior are unchanged.

## Isolated explicit-input allocation proposals — actual completed scope

### Implemented behavior and routes

Source: `finance_allocation_lab/{models,services,views,tests}.py`, its own
`migrations/0001_initial.py`, `src/FinanceAllocationLab.tsx`,
`FinanceAllocationFields.tsx`, `finance-allocation.ts` and scoped CSS.
The lab-only URLConf exposes `/lab/allocations/` (GET/POST) and
`/lab/allocations/<id>/` (GET/PUT). `/lab-allocation-ui/` renders the distinct
worksheet. The normal ERP has none of these routes.

Reviewer path: run the existing **disposable** Finance facility locally, open
`/lab-ui/`, use **Open isolated synthetic test session**, configure synthetic
draft account/dimension choices if absent, then follow **Allocation proposals**.
Direct unauthenticated allocation entry links back to that session facility;
it does not create accounts, authenticate silently, seed or grant access.
The runner's synthetic actor is nonstaff/nonsuperuser, has an unusable password
and zero grants. No credentials are required or published.

Enter an explicit source amount, currency, proposed date and explanation
(2,000-character limit), plus one or more destination amounts with saved draft
accounts and optional BU/dimensions. Date/currency are not defaulted. Only QAR
is implemented; other currencies are rejected, not converted. The source and
each destination must be positive, finite exact amounts within the existing
draft field limit and at most two decimal places. Invalid/ambiguous IDs,
foreign-entity choices, invalid dates, unknown allocation conventions and
over-allocation produce actionable validation without partial writes.

Python Decimal and frontend BigInt cents compute the exact allocated total and
source-minus-allocated difference. Positive remainder is clearly **remaining,
not fully allocated**; negative review is **overallocated by**, not mislabeled
as a remaining amount. Overallocated proposals cannot be saved; an underallocated
proposal may be saved explicitly as a draft. No percentage, basis, tax/FX,
recognition, residual distribution or account mapping is selected.

Debit/credit lines are explicitly entered **separately** from allocation
destinations. They use existing account/entity/BU/dimension and money validators.
Review uses the existing minimum-two-lines, positive-one-side and balanced-total
criteria. The API can preserve an unbalanced proposal for review; the UI follows
the existing balanced-review-before-save gate. Journal balance is not automatic
reconciliation to a source/accounting mapping and does not authorize posting.
No balancing line, operational journal, schedule, import or posting is generated.

Save/reopen/edit persists actual disposable PostgreSQL rows, not session-only
browser state. Each save preserves a complete immutable snapshot. Row locks and
expected revisions prevent lost updates; HTTP 409 retains local work until an
explicit confirmed saved-version reload. A failed list refresh does not turn a
committed save into a claimed failure. Unknown save outcomes block resubmission/
new replacement proposals and direct the reviewer to refresh/reopen; there is
no automatic retry. Navigation retains the existing before-unload protection.
English internal labels coexist with preserved supplied Arabic business titles,
explanations and line memos. Customer document presentation is unchanged.

### Isolation and schema

Allocation models are in a **separate app**, added only by
`config.finance_lab_settings`. Its migration creates proposal/revision tables
and an UPDATE/DELETE-rejecting immutable-history trigger in disposable
PostgreSQL. Both models have `default_permissions=()`; no permission/admin
powers are introduced. There is no new migration in `foundation/migrations`.

The existing guarded session checks explicit lab mode, active designated test
actor, synthetic entity, loopback/test database and matching independently owned
PostgreSQL data directory on requests. Normal settings do not install this app.
The focused test removes it from the registry and loads the normal migration
graph **without a DB connection**, proving no allocation migration node and
zero queries. This avoids adding another shared-startup schema dependency.
No existing shared migration, record, account, credential, grant, financial
control, privacy setting or service was changed. No production integration,
publication or purchase occurred. Existing preview recovery is separate;
FINANCE_PREVIEW_RECOVERY_ASSESSMENT.md was not edited or executed.

## Isolated budget scenario proposals — completed implementation and evidence

### Actual user journey and boundaries

Sources: `finance_allocation_lab/budget.py`, `budget_views.py`, `models.py`,
`migrations/0002_budget_scenarios.py`, `test_budgets.py`;
`src/FinanceBudgetLab.tsx`, `finance-budget.ts`, `finance-budget.css`,
`finance-budget-ui.test.tsx`;
`scripts/finance-budget-real-browser.test.mjs`. Entry integration:
`FinanceDraftLab.tsx`, `prototypes/finance-drafts/main.tsx` and the **lab-only**
`foundation.finance_lab_urls`. Normal ERP routes and settings do not expose it.

Reviewer path in the existing explicitly disposable facility:
`/lab-ui/` → **Open isolated synthetic test session** → configure/reuse saved
synthetic draft account/dimension choices → **Open isolated budget scenario
worksheet** → `/lab-budget-ui/`. The page does not open a session, seed choices
or create configuration automatically. Missing choices direct the reviewer to
the existing draft lab. No shared credentials or permission changes are needed
or provided; this is the existing guarded synthetic test-session facility, not
ordinary Finance password login or approved shared-user authority.

The worksheet is distinct from the session-only sample and from the journal/
allocation editors. A reviewer names a draft scenario and explicitly enters its
inclusive start/end date bounds, then adds/edits/removes 1–100 rows. Each row
has explicit start/end dates, exact non-negative QAR amount (existing money
validator: maximum 999999999999.99, at most two decimal places), saved draft
account, optional same-entity BU/dimension choices and optional explanation
(2,000 characters). Zero is permitted. QAR is fixed and visible; no FX.
Rows must fit the user-entered scenario bounds; no fiscal calendar, periods,
recognition, distribution, account mapping or actual financial data is inferred.
Invalid dates/ranges, precision/non-finite amounts, ambiguous IDs, foreign entity/
BU/dimension choices and unsupported inferred fields are rejected without writes.

Exact Python Decimal / frontend bigint cents totals count each entered amount
once. They are **proposed input totals**, not spending authority, accounting
balance, actuals or approved budgets. No journal balancing/offset is required
or generated. No proposal value is fed into operational `ReportBudget` or sales/
budget-actual reports. Existing reports and examples remain untouched.

For identical account/BU/dimension sets, equal entered dates and amounts produce
a duplicate advisory; other inclusive date intersections produce an overlap
advisory. The frontend/server agree on monetary equality. All original amounts/
explanations remain; warnings neither reject nor consolidate/prorate rows.
Different BU/dimension coordinates are not merged. The UI explicitly states
that this is reviewer information, not company acceptance policy.

POST/PUT and immutable snapshots are one atomic transaction. List is deterministically
ordered by updated timestamp then ID descending; detail/history is coherent under
the row lock. GET creates no business rows. Actual persistence survives page
reload and reopening during the disposable session. `expected_revision` plus row
locking rejects concurrent stale edits with 409, preserving the winner intact.
The UI keeps the loser's inputs and requires confirmation before replacing them
with the saved version. Unknown network/HTTP5xx save outcomes block blind save/
new-scenario retries pending explicit list/reopen recovery. Successful saves are
not mislabeled failures if an unrelated list refresh fails. Confirmed 403 clears
protected inputs/register/history, including post-commit list refresh denial;
unrelated failures preserve work. Existing unsaved/pending unload protection
remains. English labels preserve user-supplied Arabic names/explanations.
